The   cover   visual   embodies   the   theme   “Resilient   Growth” 
A  towering  tree  rooted  in  a  rocky  cliff  symbolises  strength,  
adaptability  and  sustainable  growth.  The  upward  perspective  
reflects   Sunway   REIT’s   forward-looking   strategy,   while   lush   
greenery   signifies   renewal   and   Environmental,   Social   and   
Governance  (“ESG”)  integration.  The  rocky  base  reinforces  a  
solid   foundation,   highlighting   stability   and   consistent   value   
creation. Together, the imagery conveys Sunway REIT’s journey 
of    strengthening    its    roots    while    reaching    toward    future    
opportunities.

Reporting Scope and Boundary 
This report covers Sunway REIT’s financial and non-financial performance for the period 
from  1  January  2025  to  31  December  2025,  unless  stated  otherwise.  The  scope  includes  
all  business  entities,  assets  and  operations  under  the  Trust’s  full  operational  control,  
including subsidiaries.
Basis of Preparation
Disclosures have been further scoped based on the principle of materiality of information 
as well as the disclosure requirements set out in the following reporting frameworks: 
For detailed information on materiality determination, kindly refer to the Sunway REIT 
Sustainability Report 2025, which outlines the materiality assessment process and the 
identification and prioritisation of material issues. The approach to materiality is guided 
by the following considerations:
• Mandatory  disclosures  required  to  comply  with  regulatory  frameworks  such  as  
Bursa Malaysia’s enhanced sustainability reporting requirements and the NSRF.
• Adoption of IFRS S1 and S2 standards.
• Information needs of capital providers and other stakeholders, including unitholders.
Where  relevant,  GRI  reporting  principles  have  been  applied  to  ensure  meaningful  
disclosures.     These     include     stakeholder     inclusiveness,     sustainability     context,     
completeness, balance, comparability, accuracy, timeliness, reliability and clarity.

Sunway  REIT’s  portfolio  is  concentrated  in  Sunway  City  Kuala  Lumpur,  home  
to  its  flagship  asset,  Sunway  Pyramid  Mall.  Other  properties  in  the  township  
include  Sunway  Resort  Hotel,  Sunway  Pyramid  Hotel,  Sunway  Lagoon  Hotel,  
Sunway Pinnacle and Menara Sunway.
In  Kuala  Lumpur  city  centre,  the  Trust  owns  six  assets:  Sunway  163  Mall,  
Sunway REIT Hypermarket - Ulu Kelang, Sunway Tower and and a three-in-one 
integrated property called Sunway Putra which consists of Sunway Putra Mall, 
Sunway Putra Hotel and Sunway Putra Tower.
Within Selangor, the portfolio comprises eight properties: Sunway Pier (which 
is planned for redevelopment into a retail-centric tourist destination), Wisma 
Sunway,  Sunway  REIT  Industrial  –  Shah  Alam  1,    Sunway  REIT  Industrial  –  
Petaling  Jaya  1  and  four  Sunway  REIT  Hypermarkets  located  in  Kinrara,  Putra  
Heights, USJ and Klang.
In the northern region, Sunway REIT holds six assets across Perak and Penang. 
These  include  SunCity  Ipoh  Hypermarket  and  the  newly  acquired  AEON  Mall  
Seri Manjung in Perak, as well as Sunway Hotel Seberang Jaya, Sunway Hotel 
Georgetown, Sunway Carnival Mall and Sunway REIT Industrial – Prai in Penang.
In the southern region, the portfolio includes two properties in Johor: Sunway 
Kluang Mall and Sunway REIT Hypermarket – Plentong.
Sunway  REIT  adopts  a  strategic  diversification  approach  across  asset  types,  
sectors  and  geographies  to  reduce  reliance  on  any  single  asset  class.  This  
strategy  strengthens  its  resilience,  enables  it  to  capture  emerging  growth  
opportunities and maximises operational synergies across the portfolio.

MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN
OPERATING ENVIRONMENT
The   year   2025   unfolded   against   a   backdrop   of   
evolving  global  and  domestic  economic  dynamics,  
with moderate growth, lingering geopolitical tensions 
and   shifting   investor   sentiment   shaping   the   real   
estate investment landscape. 
Global  economic  growth,  while  uneven,  expanded  by   
2.8  –  3.3%  in  2025,  according  to  the  International  
Monetary     Fund,     reflecting     some     resilience     in     
consumption     and     investment     despite     ongoing     
geopolitical    and    trade    uncertainties.    Continued    
monetary  easing  by  major  central  banks,  including  
a  series  of  interest  rate  reductions  in  the  United  
States,    contributed    to    lower    global    borrowing    
costs,   encouraged   portfolio   reallocations   toward   
emerging  markets  and  supported  sentiment  across

yield-sensitive   asset   classes.   Lower   policy   rates   
in  advanced  economies  also  alleviated  some  cost  
pressures  for  corporations  and  supported  demand  
for investment in real assets.
In   Malaysia,   domestic   macroeconomic   conditions   
demonstrated     resilience     against     these     global     
headwinds. The economy expanded by 5.2% in 2025, 
surpassing   the   5.1%   recorded   in   2024,   supported    
by    sustained    domestic    demand,    stable    private    
investment  and  a  recovery  in  export  performance.  
In    addition,    Bank    Negara    Malaysia    lowered    the    
Overnight  Policy  Rate  (“OPR”)  to  2.75  %  in  July  2025  
as a pre-emptive move to support economic activity 
amid  external  uncertainties  and  moderate  inflation.  
This  accommodative  stance  helped  maintain  credit  
growth and domestic spending.
Concurrently,  the  Malaysian  ringgit  strengthened  against  the  U.S.  dollar,  reflecting  
improved  investor  confidence  and  narrowing  interest  rate  differentials  as  U.S.   
rates  eased.  A  stronger  ringgit  helped  moderate  the  cost  of  imported  goods  
and  eased  inflationary  pressures  while  enhancing  Malaysia’s  external  purchasing  
power.  The  combination  of  a  supportive  monetary  policy,  strengthening  currency  
and resilient growth dynamics contributed to a macroeconomic environment that 
supported domestic consumption and investment flows.
In terms of challenges, businesses saw a rise in operating costs mainly due to the 
ongoing implementation of economic reforms. This included an increased minimum 
wage,   mandatory   Employees   Provident   Fund   (“EPF”)   contributions   for   foreign   
workers, the expanded scope of the sales and service tax (“SST”) and adjustments 
to energy tariffs that came into effect in the middle of 2025. While these reforms 
are intended to foster a more equitable and sustainable economic framework while 
broadening  the  tax  base,  they  have  also  tempered  near-term  activity  in  certain  
sectors.
For  Sunway  REIT,  the  electricity  tariff  restructuring  provided  some  cost  savings  
given  the  conducive  and  supportive  crude  oil  price  environment  in  FY2025  which  
determines  the  cost  of  electricity  generation.  Meanwhile,  most  of  our  service  
contractors  and  employees  are  already  compensated  above  the  minimum  wage  
level, limiting the additional wage burden.
On  the  demand  side,  many  tenants  -  particularly  small  and  medium  enterprises  
-  faced  margin  pressures  due  to  elevated  input  costs.  In  addition,  the  expansion  
of  SST  to  include  rental  or  leasing  services  for  commercial  properties  increased  
tenants’   cost   burden   and   constrained   landlords’   ability   to   raise   rents   in   the    
short-term.  A  2%  reduction  in  the  SST  on  rental  or  leasing  services,  effective   
1 January 2026, is expected to provide some cost relief to businesses.
Looking   towards   2026,   global   economic   conditions   are   expected   to   remain    
moderate   but   supportive   of   investment   in   real   assets,   although   geopolitical   
developments  in  the  Gulf  may  continue  to  introduce  some  uncertainty  around  
oil  supply  conditions,  inflationary  pressures  and  global  interest  rate  movements.  
Domestically,  Malaysia’s  growth  trajectory  into  2026  is  underpinned  by  stable  
economic   fundamentals   and   supportive   fiscal   policy.   Budget   2026   prioritises   
tourism,  infrastructure  investment  and  measures  to  stimulate  domestic  demand,  
reinforcing   an   expansionary   stance   that   aims   to   sustain   growth   momentum   
under  the  Ekonomi  MADANI  framework.  Allocations  to  the  Visit  Malaysia  Year  
2026   campaign   and   related   tourism   initiatives   are   expected   to   boost   visitor   
arrivals, retail footfall and hospitality demand, which are expected to have positive  
spill-over  effects  on  segments  of  the  real  estate  sector,  including  retail-oriented  
REITs. However, we remain cautiously optimistic as geopolitical tensions may pose 
downside risks to tourism growth.
In term of industry developments, the preferential withholding tax concession for income distributions by Malaysian Real Estate Investment 
Trusts (“M-REITs”) ended on 31 December 2025 pursuant to the Finance Act 2025. From 2026 onwards, income distributions from M-REITs that 
are exempt under Section 61A of the Income Tax Act will be taxable to the unitholders as follows:

In   2025,   M-REITs   demonstrated   resilience   and   defensive   strength   amid   a   volatile   market    
environment.  The  Bursa  Malaysia  REIT  Index  recorded  an  annual  increase  of  8.3%,  outperforming   
the broader FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI, which posted a modest increase of 2.3%. This outperformance 
was   supported   by   stable   rental   income,   attractive   dividend   yields   and   the   diversified   asset    
portfolio. Despite cost inflation and interest rate pressures earlier in the year, M-REITs with strong 
governance   and   disciplined   capital   management   and   diversified   portfolios   navigated   these   
challenges effectively, delivering sustainable performance.
Investor  confidence  in  M-REITs  as  a  defensive  asset  class  with  stable  income  strengthened   
significantly during the year. This was reflected in a notable expansion in market capitalisation, which 
surged  by  more  than  21%  to  RM59.3  billion  in  2025,  from  RM48.9  billion  in  2024.  This  growth  was  
driven by active asset acquisitions across key sectors, particularly in retail and industrial segments. 
The  recovery  in  retail  fundamentals  has  further  aided  by  the  rebound  in  tourism  and  stronger  
domestic  consumption,  underpinned  by  a  supportive  macroeconomic  environment  and  broader  
economic recovery.
M-REITs  delivered  a  stable  distribution  yield  of  5.8%,  unchanged  from  2024  due  to  the  increase  
in  unit  price  despite  the  higher  average  income  distribution  per  unit.  Total  returns  improved  from  
9.4%  in  2024  to  10.7%  in  2025,  reflecting  continued  investor  optimism  amid  easing  interest  rates  
and strong operating performances across key sectors. Furthermore, the average discount-to-Net 
Asset Value (“NAV”) narrowed from 18.5% as at 31 December 2024 to 13.5% as at 31 December 2025, 
highlighting the positive impact of higher unit prices and growing market confidence in the sector.

PROGRESS UNDER TRANSCEND 2027
Following  the  recalibration  of  our  TRANSCEND  2027  strategy  in  2024,  the  focus  in  2025  remained  on  disciplined  execution  within  the   
refined  strategic  parameters.  The  shift  from  broad  diversification  to  a  more  concentrated  emphasis  on  core  retail  and  integrated  
developments continued to guide our investment decisions. This approach supported stability in portfolio performance while maintaining 
flexibility to pursue growth opportunities in segments that align with our long-term direction.
In  2025,  we  intensified  capital  deployment  into  key  retail  and  integrated  assets  to  strengthen  their  positioning  through  improvements  in  
tenant mix, customer engagement and operating efficiency. These initiatives reflect our intention to ensure that strategic assets remain 
competitive and continue to deliver consistent income. At the same time, the criteria for opportunistic expansion introduced in 2024 was 
applied with greater selectivity. Prospective acquisitions were evaluated not only on financial merit but also on their green building credentials 
or their potential to achieve certification within three years after acquisition. This approach aligns TRANSCEND 2027 with evolving market 
expectations while supporting our sustainability roadmap.
Looking ahead, we will continue to engage regularly with our Sponsor to monitor the progress and readiness of identified pipeline of assets 
for potential injection into Sunway REIT, in line with our long-term aspiration to grow assets under management to at least RM14 billion. In 
parallel,  we  will  focus  on  organic  growth  by  maintaining  close  oversight  of  our  ongoing  asset  enhancement  initiatives  and  development  
projects which are expected to be yield accretive to our portfolio and to provide the next phase of growth for Sunway REIT.

Linking Sustainability Performance to Capital Management
In tandem with these disclosures, we have leveraged on the robust Sustainability-Linked Financing (“SLF”) Framework 
established in 2024. The adoption of this Gold-rated framework by RAM Sustainability reflects our strong governance 
and  readiness,  providing  the  structured  accountability  underpinning  our  2025  reporting.  By  linking  our  capital  
management  strategy  to  environmental  performance,  we  ensure  a  clear  alignment  between  our  sustainability  
stewardship and financial resilience.
Enhancing Physical Resilience Across the Portfolio
We  also  remain  focused  on  the  physical  resilience  of  our  assets.  We  have  allocated  RM2  million  for  an  Asset  
Enhancement  Initiative  (“AEI”)  at  Sunway  REIT  Industrial  –  Shah  Alam  1  specifically  for  flood  mitigation,  with  RM1.48  
million  already  invested  in  robust  protection  features.  This  targeted  investment  addresses  potential  exposures  
identified in our scenario analysis, where total potential flood exposure across the portfolio is estimated at RM286 
million under the worst-case scenario assuming all Sunway REIT’s properties are flooded simultaneously.
Benchmarking Against Global Environmental, Social and Governance (“ESG”) Standards
We  continue  to  benchmark  our  ESG  performance  through  global  standards.  Our  FTSE  Russell  ESG  score  improved  
from ESG Grading Band 3 in 2024 to Band 4 in 2025, leading to our inclusion in the FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia Index 
in  December  2025  after  passing  the  liquidity  requirement.  Whilst  we  maintained  an  ‘A’  rating  from  MSCI,  a  ‘B-’  for  
Water  Security  and  a  ‘C’  for  Climate  Change  from  CDP,  our  Global  Real  Estate  Sustainability  Benchmark  (“GRESB”)  
rating  was  adjusted  from  4-star  to  3-star  due  to  data  gaps  from  our  newly  acquired  properties.  This  gap  has  since  
been  addressed  through  comprehensive  tenant  data  collection  with  the  aim  to  regain  a  higher  rating  in  the  next  
assessment cycle.

OUR MARKET LANDSCAPE
FY2025   was   shaped   by   resilient   domestic   economic   expansion   
despite   a   challenging   global   backdrop.   Global   economic   growth   
moderated    as    inflationary    pressures    persisted,    interest    rates    
remained   volatile   and   geopolitical   developments   continued   to   
reshape  trade  dynamics.  Within  Malaysia,  the  economy  remained  
healthy,   charting   growth   of   5.2%   underpinned   by   strengthened   
tourism  initiatives,  boosted  domestic  consumption  and  Malaysia’s  
improved     competitive     standing     as     a     regional     investment      
destination.  Despite  this  and  a  strong  Ringgit,  consumer  sentiment  
remained cautious due to rising costs and uncertainties from policy 
adjustments.
For    Sunway    REIT,    we    experienced    tighter    operating    margins,    
heightened   cost   sensitivity   among   tenants   and   more   cautious   
leasing   dynamics   across   selected   segments   of   the   real   estate   
sector.   Inflationary   pressures,   labour   cost   adjustments,   shifts   in   
consumer   behaviour   and   regulatory   changes   further   increased   
complexity.  Notably,  the  introduction  of  an  8%  Sales  and  Service   
Tax  (“SST”)  on  commercial  rentals  and  a  6%  SST  on  construction  
services   affected   the   tenants’   occupancy   costs   and   our   asset   
enhancement  feasibilities.  Despite  these  challenges,  our  diversified  
portfolio and proactive asset management approach enabled us to 
maintain stability and protect long-term unitholder value.
Cost management remained a key priority throughout the year. The 
higher  tax  burden  on  rentals  required  a  balanced  and  collaborative  
approach to tenant engagement and rental sustainability, while rising 
construction   costs   necessitated   more   rigorous   project   controls   
and  value  engineering.  These  impacts  were  substantially  mitigated  
through  active  project  management  and  close  engagement  with  
tenants,  particularly  across  our  retail  portfolio  where  established  
relationships proven to be beneficial. While the new electricity tariff 
implemented by Tenaga Nasional Berhad effective from 1 July 2025 
provided  some  relief  on  utility  costs,  additional  opportunities  for  
efficiency,  structural  cost  improvements  and  operational  resilience  
continued to be prioritised.

Case Study: Asset Enhancement Initiative at Sunway Carnival Mall
Since 2023, Sunway REIT has committed approximately RM1 billion to three major AEIs aimed at unlocking value, strengthening income 
streams and elevating overall portfolio quality. These projects form an important part of our long-term strategy, as we reposition key 
assets, refine tenant mixes and enhance the overall experience across our properties.
The  first  initiative  involved  the  RM190  million  refurbishment  of  the  Oasis  precinct  at  Sunway  Pyramid  Mall,  carried  out  between  the   
third quarter of 2023 and the fourth quarter of 2024. The impact was immediate and visible. Footfall increased 10%, while the average 
rental rate per sq.ft. rose around 250%. This improvement translated into a higher valuation for the asset, which increased from RM3.9 
billion in 2023 to RM4.2 billion in 2024, demonstrating how targeted upgrades can elevate both operating performance and asset value.
Building  on  this  momentum,  the  second  initiative  focused  on  the  RM360  million  refurbishment  of  the  old  wing  at  Sunway  Carnival  
Mall. Work began in the third quarter of 2023, and the opening was brought forward to the second quarter of 2025. The refreshed mall 
environment has attracted stronger customer traffic, reflecting a more compelling tenant mix and improved retail experience.
The third major project, Sunway Pier, represents a new growth platform for the portfolio. This RM462 million seafront development in  
Port Klang is designed as a distinctive retail and lifestyle destination featuring a seafood market, recreational facilities and a curated 
range of food and beverage offerings. RM82 million has been invested to date, with completion targeted for the second half of 2028. 
Once operational, the project will introduce a tourism-oriented retail destination and enhance the portfolio’s growth profile.
Beyond  these  major  projects,  we  continue  to  optimise  lower-yielding  precincts  through  targeted  repositioning  and  tenant  refresh  
initiatives. These efforts introduce concepts and services aligned with evolving consumer preferences, supporting stronger occupancy 
quality and more sustainable rental performance.
Enhancements Across Key Asset Classes
Within the retail segment, ongoing works at Sunway Pyramid Mall include toilet upgrades along with scheduled air handling unit and 
lift  retrofitting,  all  aimed  at  improving  operational  efficiency  and  customer  comfort.  At  Sunway  Carnival  Mall,  the  refurbishment  was  
completed in May 2025, marking another milestone in the mall’s repositioning journey.
In the hotel segment, Sunway REIT is pursuing a strategic property development initiative following the proposed disposal of Sunway 
Hotel  Seberang  Jaya.  A  new  Sunway  Hotel  Seberang  Jaya  will  be  built  atop  Sunway  Carnival  Mall,  with  construction  commenced  in  
the fourth quarter of 2025 and completion targeted in end-2027. The new property will feature upgraded facilities, including a larger 
ballroom,  an  infinity  swimming  pool  and  direct  connectivity  to  the  mall,  creating  a  more  competitive  and  higher-yielding  integrated  
asset in mainland Penang.
Additional  enhancements  across  the  hotel  portfolio  include  switchgear  replacement  at  Sunway  Hotel  Georgetown,  compliance  and

transformer upgrades at Sunway Putra Hotel, as well as the rollout of digital in-room dining and a 24-hour live chat service at Sunway 
Resort Hotel to enhance guest experience and operational efficiency.
Enhancement  initiatives  continued  across  the  office  as  well  as  industrial  &  others  segments  to  strengthen  asset  quality,  reliability  
and  tenant  experience.  Sunway  Putra  Tower  underwent  facility  upgrades,  including  interior  and  exterior  improvements,  alongside  
the  introduction  of  2,500  sq.ft.  of  communal  space  known  as  Connect  @33  and  enhanced  amenities  such  as  modern  workstations  
and  meeting  rooms.  Elevator  upgrades  were  completed  at  Sunway  REIT  Industrial  -  Petaling  Jaya  1  and  are  currently  in  progress  at  
Wisma Sunway, improving operational reliability and tenant comfort. In addition, electric vehicle charging stations have been installed 
across our retail and office portfolio to support the growing demand of sustainable mobility. Within the industrial & others segment, 
enhancement  works  at  Sunway  REIT  Industrial  -  Prai  consist  of  repainting,  replacement  of  air  conditioning  coils  and  rectification  of  
water leakage issues, improving overall asset condition and tenant satisfaction. At Sunway REIT Industrial - Petaling Jaya 1, additional 
Net Lettable Area (“NLA”) is being created through the conversion of rooftop space into pickleball courts, with completion scheduled 
for the second half of 2026.
These AEIs form a forward-looking asset enhancement programme that strengthens portfolio quality and unlocks embedded value.  
Each upgrade and new property development decision is designed to improve income resilience, maintain asset relevance and position 
Sunway REIT for sustainable long-term growth.
TRANSFORMATIVE ASSET ENHANCEMENT INITIATIVES (“AEIs”)
In May 2025, Sunway REIT completed the RM360 million refurbishment 
of  the  old  wing  at  Sunway  Carnival  Mall,  as  part  of  its  broader  AEI  to  
reposition  the  property  as  the  leading  retail  destination  in  northern  
Malaysia. The project was completed two months ahead of schedule 
with a total NLA of approximately 761,000 sq.ft..
Located   at   Seberang   Jaya   in   mainland   Penang,   Sunway   Carnival   
Mall  serves  communities  across  mainland  Penang,  southern  Kedah  
and  northern  Perak.  The  mall  continues  to  attract  a  growing  visitor  
base  from  neighbouring  states,  alongside  increasing  international  
patronage, particularly from Chinese tourists and Indonesian medical 
travellers. This underscores Penang’s emergence as a key healthcare 
and leisure hub in the northern region. 
The  refurbishment  strategically  elevated  the  mall’s  design  and  retail  
offering,  transforming  it  from  a  community-focused  asset  into  a  
mixed-tier shopping destination with enhanced spatial efficiency and 
visitor flow. Upon completion of the refurbishment, the enhanced mall 
achieved  an  average  occupancy  rate  of  98%  with  improved  overall  
rental  rate  by  3%  in  FY2025  and  introduced  a  curated  tenant  mix  
anchored by international and lifestyle brands such as Tommy Hilfiger, 
Coach, Michael Kors, Urban Republic and KKV, strengthening Sunway  
Carnival   Mall’s   positioning   within   the   competitive   northern   retail   
landscape and bridging the gap between mass-market and premium 
retail segments.
The  design  strategy  also  delivered  a  seamless  integration  between  
the  old  and  new  wings,  ensuring  a  consistent  shopping  experience  
and  maintaining  rental  parity  across  the  entire  mall.  The  improved  
layouts   are   creating   more   efficient   retail   spaces,   encouraging    
shopper  visitations  and  contributing  to  stronger  rental  yields,  tenant  
attraction  and  tenant  retention.  Rental  reversions  are  expected  to  
exceed   projections   given   ongoing   tenant   upgrades,   while   nearly   
all  tenants  operate  under  a  revenue  sharing  model  that  enhances  
alignment between tenant success and rental growth. 
Looking   ahead,   Sunway   Carnival   Mall   exemplifies   Sunway   REIT’s   
continued    emphasis    to    future-proofing    retail    assets    through    
strategic  reinvestment,  data-driven  leasing  and  sustainable  asset   
management.    The    property    now    serves    as    a    benchmark    for    
secondary-market retail transformation, underscoring the Manager’s 
long-term  strategy  to  drive  sustainable  value  creation  across  its  
portfolio.

2026 OUTLOOK
The  operating  environment  in  2026  is  expected  to  present  a  mix  of  opportunities  and  challenges,  shaped  by  global  geopolitical  and   
economic  developments,  evolving  trade  policies  and  domestic  policy  adjustments,  including  the  expiration  of  preferential  withholding  
tax  treatment  for  REIT  distributions.  A  stronger  Malaysian  Ringgit  may  offer  cost  and  balance  sheet  advantages,  while  the  US  interest  rate  
environment  continues  to  influence  global  capital  flows.  In  this  setting,  Sunway  REIT  will  stay  focused  on  selective  acquisitions,  proactive  
asset enhancement initiatives, active asset management, disciplined capital management and close collaboration with tenants. The priorities  
are clear: protect portfolio performance, enhance asset quality and deliver stable distributions, guided by the TRANSCEND 2027 strategy.
Within   the   retail   segment,   efforts   will   centre   on   deeper   digital   transformation,   broaden   food   and   beverage   offerings   and   space    
reconfiguration  for  high-performing  tenants  across  the  malls.  These  initiatives  are  expected  to  reinforce  the  appeal  of  our  malls  and  
support  healthy  footfall  and  tenant  demand.  Cost  discipline  and  the  transition  toward  lower-carbon  assets  will  be  continued,  strengthening   
operational efficiency and long-term asset relevance.
In the hotel segment, priorities include digital marketing, international business development, dynamic pricing strategies, automation initiatives 
and  expansion  into  new  demand  segments.  These  efforts  are  supported  by  opportunities  arising  from  Visit  Malaysia  Year  2026,  which  is  
expected  to  provide  a  positive  boost  to  travel  demand  and  occupancy  levels  although  we  take  cognisant  that  in  the  event  of  a  protracted  
Middle East conflict, tourism growth may be affected in the short-term.
The  office  portfolio  will  focus  on  occupancy  recovery,  pricing  flexibility,  yield  enhancement  and  progressive  upgrades  to  facilities  and  
sustainability standards. Demand for industrial assets is expected to stay resilient, supported by Malaysia’s industrial development policies and 
evolving supply chain dynamics, which continue to attract investment into logistics and manufacturing activities.
Sunway REIT enters 2026 with a clear direction, supported by a resilient portfolio and a disciplined execution framework. A consistent focus 
on operational excellence, prudent capital deployment and long-term value creation provides a strong platform to capture opportunities and 
deliver sustainable returns for our unitholders.

While acquisitions and asset enhancement initiatives strengthened the asset portfolio of Sunway REIT, organic growth across existing 
assets continued to play an important role in the overall financial performance. Each segment navigated unique operating conditions 
during  the  year,  requiring  focused  asset  management  and  targeted  responses  to  sustain  occupancy,  rental  growth  and  tenant  
satisfaction.
In  the  retail  segment,  consumer  sentiment  softened  during  the  second  quarter  of  FY2025  amid  global  and  domestic  economic  
uncertainties. This segment also faced cost pressures linked to inflation and the introduction of the SST on rentals. E-commerce activity 
expanded,  while  changes  in  mobility  patterns  influenced  footfall  and  car  park  traffic  across  certain  locations.  These  developments  
required  more  agile  leasing  strategies  and  careful  tenant  curation  to  sustain  vibrancy  across  our  malls.  Through  active  engagement  
with tenants, targeted promotions and ongoing tenant refresh initiatives, the retail portfolio continued to deliver resilient occupancy 
and stable rental performance.
The  hotel  segment  experienced  softer  occupancy  and  lower  meetings,  incentives,  conferences  and  exhibitions  and  banqueting  
activity during the first half of FY2025. Travel patterns were affected by geopolitical tensions, shifting travel restrictions and increased 
competition from both new hotel openings and budget operators. The temporary closure of airspaces across the Middle East during 
a key travel period in June 2025 further disrupted travel flows. These factors placed pressure on occupancy and revenue per available 
room. As a result of various government-led initiatives such as progressive visa liberation and Malaysia serving as ASEAN Chair in 2025, 
tourist arrivals to Malaysia reached 26.6 million in 2025, compared with 25.0 million in 2024, reflecting a 6% increase year-on-year. This 
gradual improvement in travel demand provided a more conducive operating environment in the later part of the year.
In the office segment, new office supply of approximately 2 million sq.ft. annually, coupled with evolving workspace preferences such 
as  hybrid  working  arrangements,  influenced  occupancy  and  leasing  dynamics.  Inflation  and  regulatory  policies  also  contributed  to  
higher  maintenance  and  operating  costs.  At  Sunway  Putra  Tower,  the  departure  of  a  major  tenant  in  2024  resulted  in  its  occupancy  
falling below 70%. Our leasing efforts have yielded positive results, with secured occupancy for Sunway Putra Tower exceeding 80% at  
end-2025.
The services segment operated under a triple net lease structure. Following the disposal of the Sunway university & college campus,

which was the segment’s only asset, there was no contribution from this segment from 30 September 2025 onwards.
The  industrial  &  others  segment  faced  supply  chain  disruptions  and  higher  operating  costs,  alongside  shifts  in  tenant  demand   
influenced by changes in manufacturing and logistics activity. External trade developments, including tariff-related uncertainties, also 
affected expansion plans in certain industries. Even so, our active leasing efforts have enchanced occupancy in Sunway REIT Industrial - 
Petaling Jaya 1, whereas proactive tenant engagement and operational adjustments helped improve the occupancy to 71% at end-2025, 
from 31% in the same period last year.
Across  the  portfolio,  leasing  activity  remained  active  and  disciplined.  Sunway  REIT  achieved  an  average  rental  reversion  of  8.5%  in  
FY2025, compared with 6.4% in FY2024. The improvement was largely contributed by the retail segment with the completion of Oasis 
precinct  in  November  2024  and  fully  refurbished  Sunway  Carnival  Mall  in  May  2025.  The  portfolio’s  weighted  average  lease  expiry  
moderated  to  2.6  years  at  end-2025,  compared  with  4.0  years  in  end-2024,  following  the  disposal  of  Sunway  university  &  college  
campus.
Average occupancy levels across the portfolio remained robust, supported by proactive leasing and tenant retention strategies. Retail 
occupancy stood at 98%, hotel at 65%, office at 82% and industrial & others at 87% for FY2025.
Operationally,  improvements  in  tenant  retention  and  cost  efficiency  reflected  the  effectiveness  of  our  active  asset  management   
approach  and  continuous  tenant  engagement.  These  efforts  helped  manage  operating  expenses,  sustain  occupancy  levels  and  
enhance overall portfolio quality, supporting stable income generation across the year.
Lower Gearing Level
Sunway REIT strengthened its balance sheet through proactive portfolio optimisation and targeted asset recycling  
during  the  year.  On  30  September  2025,  Sunway  REIT  completed  the  disposal  of  the  Sunway  university  &  college  
campus for a cash consideration of RM613 million, generating a net gain on disposal of approximately RM41 million.  
The transaction reflects our disciplined strategy to monetising mature assets and unlocking value through timely 
asset recycling.
The disposal proceeds aim to support yield-accretive acquisitions and asset enhancement initiatives. In the interim, 
we are optimising returns by applying the net disposal proceeds to reduce borrowings, lowering gearing from 41.4% 
before  disposal  to  39.4%  at  end-December  2025  and  generating  annual  financing  cost  savings.  This  strengthens  
our financial position and provides greater flexibility to pursue yield-accretive asset growth. 
Our  approach  to  disciplined  capital  management  will  continue  to  focus  on  gearing  optimisation,  selective  equity  
fundraising and strategic asset recycling, supporting sustainable long-term returns for unitholders.

Malaysia’s GDP is estimated by the Ministry of Finance (“MOF”) to have expanded by 5.2% in 2025, slight improvement from 5.1% 
in 2024. Growth was driven primarily by the services sector, supported by stronger household spending, higher tourist arrivals, 
and improved activity in transportation and logistics. This momentum was reinforced by government measures such as Payung 
Rahmah  and  the  Sumbangan  Asas  Rahmah  (“SARA”)  one-off  assistance,  as  well  as  progressive  visa  liberalisation  particularly  
benefiting tourists from China and India. In addition, Malaysia’s ASEAN Chairmanship in 2025 helped lift tourism and Meetings, 
Incentives,  Conferences  and  Exhibitions  (“MICE”)  activity,  benefiting  related  service  industries.  Meanwhile,  the  manufacturing  
sector  remained  supported  by  export-oriented  industries,  particularly  Electronics  and  Electrical  (“E&E”),  which  benefited  from

demand  linked  to  data  centres  and  artificial  intelligence  applications.  This  was  complemented  by  policy  support  under  the  
New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and the National Semiconductor Strategy. The construction sector also continued to expand 
strongly,  underpinned  by  large  scale  public  infrastructure  projects  under  the  Twelfth  Malaysia  Plan  (2021  to  2025),  alongside  
rising private investment in industrial facilities, commercial developments and data centres, especially in Johor and Selangor.
Looking  ahead,  the  Government  projects  GDP  growth  of  4.0%–4.5%  in  2026,  broadly  in  line  with  the  International  Monetary  
Fund’s (“IMF”) forecast of 4.6% for 2026.
MACROECONOMIC HIGHLIGHTS
Malaysia’s  retail  sector  delivered  a  softer-than-anticipated  performance  in  2025,  with  retail  sales  growth  moderating  to  2.4%,  below  the  earlier  
projection of 3.6%, according to Retail Group Malaysia (“RGM”). The underperformance was largely attributable to a subdued Q4 2025 which recorded 
growth  of  2.5%  despite  the  seasonal  uplift  typically  associated  with  year-end  festivities,  extended  school  holidays,  and  increased  tourist  arrivals.   
From  a  segmental  standpoint,  performance  was  mixed.  The  mini-market,  convenience  store,  and  cooperative  segment  stood  out  as  the  primary  
growth driver, recording a robust expansion of 13.2% for the full year. In contrast, discretionary retail categories faced significant headwinds, with the 
furniture and furnishing, home improvement, and electrical and electronics segments collectively contracting by 9.6% over the same period.
Looking ahead, RGM has projected a retail sales growth rate of 4.0% for 2026. However, this outlook remains subject to downside risks, particularly 
from persistent cost-of-living pressures among Malaysian consumers, as well as potential external uncertainties, including conflicts in the Middle 
East.

Valley retail stock.

Unemployment Rate
In  December  2025,  Malaysia’s  unemployment  rate  remained  unchanged  at  2.9%  for  the  second  consecutive  month,  
underscoring the continued resilience of the labour market. The number of unemployed persons declined marginally by 0.1%  
month-on-month,  falling  by  700  to  517,700  (November  2025:  518,400).  On  a  year-on-year  basis,  unemployment  recorded  
further improvement, decreasing by 3.9% or 20,800 from 538,500 in December 2024. Based on preliminary estimates by the 
Department of Statistics Malaysia (“DOSM”), the overall unemployment rate for 2025 stood at 3.0%.
In  the  year  to  come,  Malaysia’s  labour  market  is  expected  to  enter  2026  on  firmer  footing,  supported  by  a  combination  of  
fiscal  measures,  tourism  recovery  and  employment-driven  initiatives.  The  Budget  2026  framework  under  Ekonomi  MADANI  
places  strong  emphasis  on  labour  market  reforms,  employability  enhancement,  wage  growth  support,  and  closer  industry  
collaboration in skills development. These initiatives aim to broaden access to higher-income opportunities while supporting 
sustainable wage progression across the workforce. Collectively, such measures are anticipated to strengthen labour market 
resilience  and  encourage  broader  participation  across  both  formal  and  emerging  sectors.  In  line  with  this  outlook,  MBSB  
Research projects the unemployment rate to remain stable at 3.0% in 2026, underpinned by steady employment growth and 
continued hiring momentum within domestic-oriented service sectors.
Overnight Policy Rate (“OPR”)
Consumer Price Index (“CPI”)
Throughout  2025,  BNM  implemented  one  Overnight  Policy  Rate  (“OPR”)  cut  in  July,  lowering  it  by  25  basis  points  to  2.75%,  and  
maintained this rate throughout the remainder of the year. In its first meeting of 2026, the Monetary Policy Committee (“MPC”) 
found that the global economic conditions in 2025 were firmer than initially anticipated, supported by milder trade restrictions, 
sustained  AI-driven  technology  investments,  and  stronger  fiscal  stimulus.  Global  growth  is  expected  to  remain  resilient  
despite  potential  headwinds  from  trade  measures,  underpinned  by  steady  domestic  demand,  easing  inflationary  pressures,  
continued  technology  investment  and  accommodative  policy  settings.  Nevertheless,  risks  persist  from  escalating  geopolitical  
tensions,  increased  financial  market  volatility  and  stretched  asset  valuations,  while  upside  potential  could  emerge  from   
stronger-than-expected technology spending, less severe trade disruptions and growth-supportive policies in major economies.
Based on consensus views from RHB Research, UOB, DBS, Kenanga and Public Invest, BNM is expected to maintain a steady 
monetary policy stance through 2026, keeping the OPR at 2.75%, as the current setting remains appropriate to support growth 
amid moderate inflation and external uncertainties.
According to the latest data from the DOSM, the CPI for 2025 slowed to 1.4%, compared with 1.8% in 2024. This was supported 
by  slower  price  growth  in  several  categories:  Housing,  Water,  Electricity,  Gas  &  Other  Fuels  increased  by  1.6%  (2024:  3.0%);  
Health  rose  1.2%  (2024:  1.8%);  Recreation,  Sport  &  Culture  grew  1.1%  (2024:  1.8%);  Transport  edged  up  0.4%  (2024:  1.0%);  
and   Furnishings,   Household   Equipment   &   Routine   Household   Maintenance   increased   0.2%   (2024:   0.7%).   Meanwhile,    
Information & Communication and Clothing & Footwear recorded declines of 4.3% and 0.2%, respectively.
On the other hand, certain categories experienced higher growth, including Personal Care, Social Protection & Miscellaneous 
Goods & Services (4.4%), Insurance & Financial Services (3.4%), Restaurant & Accommodation Services (3.2%), Education (2.3%) 
and Food & Beverages (2.1%). 
According  to  Bank  Negara  Malaysia  (“BNM”),  headline  inflation  is  projected  to  remain  moderate  in  2026,  averaging  between  
1.5% and 2.5%, despite heightened global price volatility arising from ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

In  2025,  the  average  occupancy  rate  of  shopping  malls  in  the  Klang  Valley  improved  to  83.9%.  This  uptrend  signals  a  sustained  recovery  in

leasing  activity,  extending  the  positive  momentum  observed  in  the  post-pandemic  period.  The  recovery  has  been  largely  supported  by  the  
robust  performance  of  prime  retail  assets,  where  tenant  demand  has  remained  resilient.  Well-located,  top-tier  malls  continue  to  outperform  
the  broader  market,  sustaining  high  occupancy  levels  and  attracting  a  steady  influx  of  international  retailers  as  well  as  experiential  and   
lifestyle-focused  brands.  Conversely,  ageing  and  weaker-performing  malls  are  facing  growing  challenges  in  tenant  retention  and  positioning,  
underscoring an increasingly pronounced divergence in performance within the retail sector.
Despite  the  improvement  in  occupancy  levels,  net  absorption  across  the  Klang  Valley  weakened  significantly  during  the  first  nine  months  of   
2025.  Total  net  take-up  amounted  to  0.30  million  sq.ft.,  representing  a  sharp  decline  of  74.4%  compared  to  the  corresponding  period  in  2024.  
Kuala Lumpur recorded positive net absorption of 0.37 million sq.ft., although this was 29.9% lower year-on-year, while areas outside Kuala Lumpur 
experienced net space contraction of 0.07 million sq.ft., reversing the positive absorption recorded in the previous year. 
While  purpose-built  retail  occupancy  across  the  Klang  Valley  continues  to  trend  upward,  the  contraction  in  net  absorption  highlights  a  more  
cautious  leasing  environment.  This  reflects  softer  market  sentiment  amid  ongoing  concerns  over  consumer  spending.  Although  inflationary  
pressures have eased across the Klang Valley, elevated living costs continue to constrain discretionary expenditure, thereby tempering expansion 
plans among retailers and weighing on overall space take-up.

Sales and Service Tax (“SST”) Expansion Weighs on Retailers and Landlords
The expansion of Malaysia’s SST in July 2025 has heightened pressure on retail margins, particularly in discretionary and newly taxable categories. 
Higher  post-tax  prices  have  increased  consumer  price  sensitivity,  leading  to  more  cautious  spending  and  softer  transaction  volumes  in   
non-essential segments. These demand-side pressures are compounded by rising operating costs, as the new 8% SST is layered on top of higher 
labour  expenses,  including  the  increase  in  the  minimum  wage  to  RM1,700  in  February  2025  and  mandatory  Employees  Provident  Fund  (“EPF”)  
contributions for foreign workers from October 2025.
For  landlords,  the  extension  of  the  8%  SST  to  commercial  property  leasing  and  rental  services  applies  to  offices,  shopping  malls,  shop  lots  
and  warehouses.  This  is  expected  to  result  in  weaker  space  absorption  and  downward  pressure  on  rental  growth.  However,  the  government’s  
subsequent  reduction  of  the  service  tax  rate  on  rental  and  leasing  services  to  6%  in  January  2026  may  help  partially  mitigate  the  overall  tax

burden.
Source: New Strait Times (“NST”), The Edge Malaysia

Household  disposable  income  is  projected  to  increase  following  the  implementation  of  the  Civil  Service  Pay  Reform  (SSPA  Phase  2),  which  will  
inject an extra RM18 billion for 1.6 million civil servants from January 2026. In addition, the government continues to allocate funds for cash and 
welfare  assistance  through  the  Sumbangan  Tunai  Rahmah  (“STR”)  and  SARA  Madani  initiatives,  amounting  to  RM15  billion.  Part  of  this  support  
includes an additional RM100 SARA payment to 22 million Malaysians, effective from February 2026. This is expected to provide a near-term uplift 
to consumer spending, particularly during the Ramadan and Chinese New Year festive periods.

non-prime  office  to  its  headquarters  at  Menara  Alliance  Bank,  Ant  International  establishing  its  regional  base  at  The  Exchange  106,  and  Bursa  
Malaysia  reportedly  in  advanced  negotiations  to  occupy  space  within  the  same  tower  in  the  financial  district.  Maybank  has  also  confirmed  its  
phased relocation to Merdeka 118 starting in 2026. These moves underscore the growing emphasis on quality, operational efficiency, and brand 
presence in tenants’ real estate strategies.
In 2025, Klang Valley’s office stock reached 188.7 million sq.ft., reflecting a marginal year-on-year increase of approximately 0.21%. New completions 
were concentrated in decentralised locations, with key additions including Menara TNB Bangsar in the KL Fringe, as well as Sunway Square Corporate 
Towers  and  Sunsuria  Forum  in  Selangor.  According  to  Knight  Frank  Research,  these  additions  provide  a  measured  expansion  of  decentralised  
office options, offering larger, more efficient floorplates that cater to corporates seeking cost-effective locations beyond the city core, particularly 
as occupiers continue to reassess spatial requirements and focus on value-driven sites.
The office development pipeline is expected to stay active in 2026, with an estimated 2.8 million sq.ft. of new supply. Menara Golden Eagle in KL 
City is slated for completion in the first half of 2026, while delivery activity is projected to accelerate in the latter half of the year.

As  we  enter  2026,  the  Klang  Valley  office  market  is  set  to  navigate  a  period  of  measured  growth  and  selective  demand.  While  the  pipeline  of  
high-specification, large-scale developments is expected to expand supply, tenants are likely to continue favouring modern, well-located spaces 
that  offer  operational  efficiency  and  ESG-aligned  features.  This  preference  will  sustain  interest  in  Grade  A  and  premium  offices,  while  older  or  
secondary buildings may face continued pressure to offer incentives. The market enters 2026 with cautious optimism, but the elevated supply 
pipeline is expected to keep rentals relatively soft and drive more tenant-friendly conditions. 
Transforming Legacy Office Assets
As  outlined  earlier,  non-prime  and  non-green  office  buildings  continue  to  experience  elevated  vacancy  levels,  placing  sustained  downward  
pressure on occupancy across the Klang Valley. CBRE | WTW estimates that approximately 77% of the total net lettable area in the Klang Valley 
area no longer meets current market standards for performance, space efficiency, or environmental compliance, largely comprising ageing office 
towers developed prior to 2015.
The  government  has  also  recognized  this  challenge  and  introduced  measures  to  encourage  the  adaptive  reuse  and  repurposing  of  office  
buildings. Notably, Budget 2026 proposed a special tax deduction for the conversion of office assets, aimed at supporting such initiatives. While 
interest in refurbishment and conversion has gained momentum, progress remains constrained by high capital requirements, complex approval 
processes, and uncertainties surrounding demand viability and investment returns. Nonetheless, several successful precedents, including Wisma 
KFC, Menara MIDF, Wisma Lee Rubber, and the Oriental Bank Building, have been refurbished and repositioned for hospitality use. 
Source: CBRE | WTW Research & Consulting
Rise of Co-Working Spaces
Co-working  spaces  have  been  on  an  upward  trend,  supported  by  the  sustained  adoption  of  hybrid  work  models  and  growing  enterprise  
demand.  These  flexible  workspaces  have  reshaped  tenant  priorities,  offering  an  alternative  to  traditional  offices,  which  often  involve  rigid  
leases, fixed square footage, and high upfront costs that limit agility. In contrast, co-working solutions provide a capex-light, space-as-a-service 
model,  enabling  companies  to  scale  their  teams  up  or  down  quickly  without  being  locked  into  lengthy  contracts.  Supporting  this  trend,  Knight  
Frank  Research  highlights  several  notable  co-working  launches  in  2025.  Common  Ground  opened  its  flagship  15,000  sq.ft.  centre  at  Menara   
Darussalam,  Infinity8  launched  outlets  at  TRX@Exchange  and  Sunway  Square  Corporate  Towers  measuring  30,000  sq.ft.  and  24,000  sq.ft.,  
respectively, while Universal Serviced Offices expanded its footprint with the addition of 337 new workstations.

Reducing Export Uncertainty, Opening New Markets
Malaysia’s  external  trade  landscape  strengthened  significantly  following  a  series  of  strategic  trade  developments  during  and  after  the  47
th
 
ASEAN Summit. The Agreement on Reciprocal Trade (“ART”) improved market access to the United States, Malaysia’s third largest trading partner,  
reducing tariffs on Malaysian exports from 25% to 19% and granting duty exemptions for 1,711 product categories. These measures are expected 
to benefit high value sectors, particularly aerospace, E&E, and chemical and oleochemical industries.
Beyond  the  United  States,  Malaysia  continued  to  expand  its  free  trade  agreement  network.  Notable  milestones  include  the  Malaysia  EFTA  
Economic  Partnership  Agreement  (“MEEPA”)  in  June  2025,  its  first  trade  pact  with  Switzerland,  Norway,  Iceland  and  Liechtenstein,  followed  
by  the  Malaysia-Korea  Free  Trade  Agreement  (“MKFTA”)  in  October  2025.  Existing  agreements  are  also  being  modernised,  such  as  the   
Malaysia-New  Zealand  Free  Trade  Agreement  (“MNZFTA”),  while  long  stalled  negotiations  with  the  European  Union  have  been  reactivated  after  
more than a decade. With U.S. tariffs stabilised and key trade agreements in place, the operating environment for exporters is more predictable, 
reducing uncertainty and expanding access to new export markets.
Source: Knight Frank Research
Data Centre Expansion in Malaysia
Malaysia’s data centre sector is experiencing rapid growth, driven by strong foreign direct investment, government support, and rising demand  
for cloud and AI infrastructure. As of mid-2025, the country recorded RM42.6 billion in digital investments under the Malaysia Digital initiative, with 
the majority concentrated in data centres and cloud facilities. To meet demand for large and strategically located sites, landowners, including palm 
oil plantation companies, have begun allocating portions of their estates for industrial parks dedicated to data centre development, with renewable 
energy solutions such as solar and battery storage helping to sustainably meet rising power requirements. Notable projects and initiatives driving 
this growth include the Southern Johor Renewable Energy Corridor, and national programmes such as the Sustainable Data Centre Framework and 
National Cloud Computing Policy. Collectively, these trends position Malaysia as a leading destination for high-value, energy-intensive industrial 
infrastructure in Southeast Asia.

The Board of the Manager upholds robust risk management practices through an established risk management framework. This framework 
operates  on  a  three-tiered  risk  governance  and  oversight  model,  providing  a  structured  and  comprehensive  approach  to  the  timely  
identification, assessment and mitigation of risks at the origin of the risk event. At Sunway REIT, risk management is embedded across all 
core business operations and processes to ensure key risks are proactively managed in line with the Board’s risk appetite, supporting the 
achievement of financial, business and operational objectives.
The  Board  is  supported  by  the  Risk  Management  Committee  (“RMC”)  and  Risk  Management  Working  Group,  which  are  responsible  for  
reviewing  key  risks,  opportunities,  and  control  effectiveness.  The  Risk  Officer  works  closely  with  designated  risk  champions  and  risk  
owners  across  business  units  and  functional  departments  to  maintain  and  periodically  update  the  Risk  Register,  ensuring  that  identified  
risks,  including  sustainability  and  climate-related  exposures,  are  monitored,  prioritised  and  mitigated  through  appropriate  controls  and  
management action plans.

Most key risks remained stable during the financial year, with notable movements observed in acquisition and investment risk, litigation risk 
and business / market risk.
Acquisition  and  investment  risk  was  lowered  from  Moderate  to  Low  supported  by  a  set  approved  investment  criterias  approved  by  the  
Board and monitored by Investment Appraisal Working Group. Recent acquisitions in 2024 and 2025 totaling RM1.1 billion met or exceeded 
their initial yield forecasts. Litigation risk has been lowered from High to Moderate following the conclusion of the assessment of damages 
by High Court in November 2024, with no new evidence were allowed to be produced at Court of Appeal. The case has been fixed for hearing 
at the Court of Appeal on 26 January 2027.
The escalating conflicts in the Middle East in Q1 2026 has elevated the following key risks of Sunway REIT:
Firstly, Business / Market risk. The residual risk rating has been revised upward from Moderate to High, reflecting heightened uncertainty 
and  potential  spillover  effects  stemming  from  the  conflict,  which  may  adversely  impact  operating  conditions  of  our  Hotel  segment.  The  
segment may face pressure on occupancy rates as flight disruptions through Gulf transit hubs could affect approximately 7% of our guest 
base originating from Middle East (6%) and Europe (1%). In response, we are actively diversifying our guest mix by strengthening domestic 
demand and tapping into alternative international markets. While the Hotel segment may face near-term headwinds, the overall portfolio 
remains resilient. Defensive assets such as Retail, Office and Industrial & Others properties, which collectively contribute approximately 89% 
of the portfolio’s revenue, provide stability during periods of geopolitical volatility. 
Secondly,  the  Inflation  risk.  The  recent  surge  in  global  oil  prices,  approaching  US$100  per  barrel,  is  expected  to  exert  upward  pressure  on  
electricity  tariffs  and  logistics  fuel  costs,  which  may  in  turn  compress  operating  margins.  The  residual  risk  rating  remained  as  Moderate,  
although the impact has increased in view of rising cost pressures.

The retail sales per sq.ft. in 2025 recorded a marginal decline of 1% compared to the previous year, reflecting a normalisation following 
the strong recovery achieved in 2024. Performance in the first half of the year was softer, as consumer spending moderated amid more 
cautious consumer sentiment due to ongoing global economic uncertainty.
Encouragingly, retail activity improved in the second half of 2025, supported by better footfall trends and festive shopping cycles across 
Sunway REIT’s malls. The gradual improvement in consumer sentiment, coupled with ongoing mall enhancements and targeted marketing 
initiatives, contributed to the recovery in sales momentum during the latter part of the year.
Overall,  while  retail  sales  per  sq.ft.  edged  slightly  lower  on  a  full-year  basis,  the  improving  second-half  performance  underscores  the  
resilience  of  Sunway  REIT’s  retail  portfolio  and  reflects  a  stabilisation  in  consumer  spending  patterns,  supported  by  the  continued  
preference for in-person shopping experiences and the sustained attractiveness of Sunway REIT’s malls.

Following the acquisition of Sunway Pier in 2022, the Manager developed a strategic plan to transform this asset into a vibrant retail-centric 
tourism  destination.  The  redevelopment  exercise  commenced  on  29  October  2024,  with  targeted  completion  in  H2  2028.  The  change  from  
earlier planned completion in H2 2027 was due to revised layout plan and piling system. The new development will now feature an expanded 
building GFA of approximately 620,000 sq.ft. and NLA of approximately 390,000 sq.ft. along with more than 740 parking bays. 
Building on this vision of community-centric, experience-led retail, the development will reposition the former ferry terminal in Port Klang 
into a seafront lifestyle destination. The development will feature curated retail concepts alongside immersive dining experiences, including 
alfresco F&B offerings overlooking the waterfront, as well as a seafood market. Plans for the development also include public waterfront 
spaces  designed  to  encourage  community  engagement  and  recreational  activities  beyond  traditional  retail,  enhancing  Sunway  Pier’s  
positioning as a distinctive leisure and tourism destination. 
Located adjacent to the Port Klang KTM station and on the western end of the Federal Highway, Sunway Pier is easily accessible by public 
transport and is within an easy 50-minute drive from KLCC. With an estimated development cost of RM462.0 million, Sunway Pier is expected 
to strengthen Port Klang’s appeal as a destination for leisure, lifestyle and shopping activities.

AEON  Mall  Seri  Manjung,  a  freehold  two-storey  retail  complex  located  in  Seri  
Manjung, Perak was acquired for RM138.0 million, from Kar Sin Bhd. The acquisition 
was  completed  on  25  July  2025.  The  property  is  strategically  located  in  Seri   
Manjung  -  the  commercial  hub  of  the  district,  and  is  surrounded  by  mature  
residential   communities   and   key   civic   amenities,   catering   to   a   catchment   
population of over 294,000 residents in the Manjung district. 
The  property  is  single-leased  to  AEON  Co.  (M)  Bhd.  under  a  long-term  lease  
agreement and provides income stability with a remaining lease tenure of 12 years 
up to December 2037. The retail offerings include a wide spectrum of F&B outlets, 
as well as fashion and clothing stores, health and beauty services, accessories, a 
cinema and many more. The wide array of tenancy mix serves a mature residential 
market   catchment   and   in   particular   attracts   families,   students   and   working   
professionals in Manjung district. 
The  impending  completion  of  the  West  Coast  Expressway  (“WCE”)  presents  an  
exciting  opportunity  for  the  property  to  capitalise  on  the  improved  connectivity  
between Taiping and Selangor. The property also stands to benefit in the long run 
from the development of Lumut Maritime Industrial City (“LuMIC”), which aims to 
establish the nearby town, Lumut as a key maritime and industrial hub.
Building on the successful launch of the new wing in 2022, Sunway REIT commenced the asset enhancement initiative for the old wing in 
June 2023 to further optimise the mall’s average rental rate and unlock its full growth potential. With a total development cost of RM360.0 
million, the refurbishment was completed two months ahead of schedule in May 2025.
As  at  31  December  2025,  Sunway  Carnival  Mall’s  occupancy  rate  stood  at  99%,  reflecting  the  success  of  the  initiative  in  attracting   
high-yield tenants, supported by enhancements to the mall’s external façade that elevate its aesthetic appeal and seamless connectivity 
across the expanded mall, collectively creating a more inviting and engaging environment that enhances the overall shopping experience 
for consumers in mainland Penang.

Sunway  Hotel  Seberang  Jaya  –  a  4-star  202-room  hotel  located  
in  Seberang  Jaya,  Penang  is  in  the  process  of  being  disposed  of  
to  Sunway  Medical  Centre  Penang  Sdn.  Bhd.  at  a  value  of  RM60.0  
million,  with  the  conditional  sale  and  purchase  agreement  (“SPA”)  
signed  on  28  October  2025.  The  transaction  is  expected  to  be  
completed  within  2  years’  time  by  fourth  quarter  of  2027,  after  
fulfillment of the required conditions to sale. 
The hotel is strategically located in the Seberang Jaya town centre 
at  the  intersection  between  the  North-South  Expressway  and  the   
East-West Highway, and is conveniently accessible via a 40-minute 
drive  from  the  iconic  Penang  Bridge  and  Penang  International  
Airport.
Located  within  a  vibrant  hub  of  entertainment,  leisure,  medical  
facilities,   and   retail   anchored   by   the   newly   expanded   Sunway   
Carnival  Mall,  the  proposed  disposal  of  this  hotel  presents  an  
exciting   opportunity   for   the   Manager   to   realise   gains   on   its   
initial  investment  and  recycle  the  proceeds  from  disposal  for  the  
construction of a new hotel atop Sunway Carnival Mall and unlock 
significant synergies between the two assets. 
In  parallel  with  the  proposed  disposal  of  Sunway  Hotel  Seberang  
Jaya, the Manager plans to develop a new Sunway Hotel Seberang 
Jaya  atop  Sunway  Carnival  Mall,  with  an  estimated  development  
cost  of  RM140.0  million  and  targeted  completion  in  the  fourth  
quarter of 2027.
The  proposed  new  Sunway  Hotel  Seberang  Jaya  will  comprise  an  
11-storey  building  featuring  192  rooms,  a  grand  ballroom  with  a  
banquet capacity of up to 600 guests (compared with 200 guests 
at  the  existing  hotel),  meeting  rooms  and  a  rooftop  facilities  deck  
featuring an infinity swimming pool and wading pool as new lifestyle 
amenities, alongside entertainment areas and direct connectivity to 
Sunway Carnival Mall, offering upgraded and seamless experience 
for hotel guests.
Upon   completion,   the   integrated   development   is   expected   to   
enhance  the  value  of  Sunway  Carnival  Mall  by  driving  increased  
footfall  and  dwell  time,  while  simultaneously  providing  the  new  
Sunway  Hotel  Seberang  Jaya  with  a  unique  and  convenient  value  
proposition  for  its  guests,  ultimately  creating  a  more  compelling  
and  strengthening  the  overall  competitiveness  of  the  integrated  
development in mainland Penang.

connectivity which have supported the growth of the tourism sector.

comparable to that of FY2024. 
Federal Budget 2026 provides a supportive backdrop for the hospitality industry, with approximately RM700 million allocated to tourism, 
including  RM500  million  for  Visit  Malaysia  Year  2026,  alongside  tax  relief  of  up  to  RM1,000  for  domestic  travel.  These  measures  are  
anticipated to lift hotel occupancies.
The Manager remains cautiously optimistic on the outlook for the hotel segment, underpinned by positive trends in tourist arrivals as the

country  gears  up  for  Visit  Malaysia  Year  2026  with  expanding  air  connectivity,  broader  promotional  campaigns  and  enhanced  tourism  
offerings.  Notwithstanding  this,  the  Manager  acknowledges  that  any  sustained  escalation  of  conflicts  in  the  Middle  East  may  weigh  
on tourism demand. The Manager will continue to adopt a proactive pricing strategy, strengthen targeted marketing efforts and place 
greater emphasis on MICE events to enhance the performance of the hotel segment.

Between the second half of 2025 and 2026, approximately 4.4 million sq.ft. of new office supply was projected to enter the Klang Valley market, 
comprising about 1.3 million sq.ft. in H2 2025 and 3.1 million sq.ft. in 2026. Notwithstanding the increase in supply, strong leasing momentum was 
recorded, with absorption in the first nine months of 2025 exceeding that of 2024. 
The demand is primarily focused on newer, high-quality Grade A office spaces, particularly those with good accessibility to public transportation. 
Key demand drivers include the technology, financial services and professional services sectors. While new supply is being absorbed, the continued 
delivery of new office space continues to exert pressure on older buildings. 
The  stable  occupancy  of  Sunway  REIT’s  office  segment  in  FY2025  was  underpinned  by  ongoing  efforts  to  enhance  the  competitiveness  
of   the   portfolio   through   continuous   asset   enhancement   initiatives,   including   upgrades   to   air   conditioning   systems,   lifts,   transformers   
and   general   amenities   area   for   tenants.   These   improvements   are   in   line   with   Sunway   REIT’s   energy   efficiency   and   green   certification   
strategies   for   the   office   portfolio,   and   aligned   with   Federal   Budget   2026   initiatives,   promoting   the   development   of   digital   and    
ESG-compliant workspaces. 
The  office  segment  is  expected  to  remain  resilient  in  FY2026,  supported  by  committed  tenancies.  The  Manager  will  continue  to  pursue  green  
certification initiatives and offer flexible leasing solutions to enhance tenant retention and attract new occupants. 
Sunway  Putra  Tower  introduces  Connect  @33,  a  new  workspace  
designed   to   elevate   tenant   experience.   The   space   combines    
co-working zones, versatile breakout ares, and thoughtfully curated 
environments  that  encourage  focus,  collaboration  and  seamless  
interaction. 
Features    include    meeting    rooms,    hot    desk    zones,    dedicated    
workstation,  community  spaces  and  hangout  areas  to  create  a  
flexible  and  dynamic  setting  enhancing  the  overall  appeal  of  the  
office environment.
On 2 May 2025, Sunway REIT entered into a conditional sale and purchase agreement with Sunway College (KL) Sdn. Bhd., a wholly owned 
subsidiary of Sunway Education Group Sdn. Bhd., for the disposal of Sunway University & College campus for a total cash consideration of 
RM613 million.
 
Located in Sunway City Kuala Lumpur, the property comprises several academic blocks, four blocks of five-storey walk-up hostel apartments, 
and  sports  facilities.  The  disposal  consideration  represents  a  premium  of  4.6%  over  the  property’s  market  value  of  RM586  million,  as  
appraised by independent valuer Jones Lang Wootton (Proprietor: Singham Sulaiman Sdn. Bhd.) on 1 December 2024.
 
The disposal was completed on 30 September 2025, following which the property ceased contributing rental income to Sunway REIT. The 
transaction  enabled  Sunway  REIT  to  realise  a  gross  disposal  gain  of  RM49  million  over  the  total  investment  cost  of  RM564  million.  After  
accounting for incidental disposal costs of RM8 million, the net gain on disposal amounted to RM41 million.

In  line  with  growing  investments  in  Malaysia,  demand  for  industrial  
properties  is  expected  to  remain  strong.  Under  the  New  Industrial  
Master   Plan   (“NIMP”)   2030   and   the   National   Energy   Transition   
Roadmap  (“NETR”),  there  will  be  greater  emphasis  on  sustainability  
and  technological  advancements  in  industries  leading  to  increased  
demand  for  modern  premises.  Accordingly,  demand  for  industrial  
properties is expected to remain resilient especially in core locations 
like Shah Alam and Penang. 
Malaysia’s   diversified   trade   ties   and   involvement   in   Regional   
Comprehensive  Economic  Partnerships  (“RCEP”)  and  Brazil,  Russia,  
India,  China  and  South  Africa  (“BRICS”)  positions  it  well  to  capitalise  
on  global  supply  chain  realignments.  While  geopolitical  risks  persist  
–  particularly  from  US  President  Trump’s  trade  stance  and  ongoing  
US-China   tensions   –   these   shifts   offer   opportunities   for   local   
manufacturers  and  logistics  players  to  access  new  markets  and  
bodes  well  for  demand  for  factories  and  warehouses.  Domestic  
demand is also expected to continue supporting domestic-oriented 
industries  amid  sustained  local  activity.  With  the  US  tariff  set  at  
19%,  on  par  with  other  ASEAN  countries,  Malaysia’s  exports  remain  
competitive,  making  it  an  attractive  destination  for  industrial  and  
manufacturing investments.

THREE-PRONGED APPROACH
Sunway  REIT  maintained  its  track  record  of  gearing  around  40%  of  total  asset  value  in  FY2025,  within  the  50%  limit  
allowed under the Listed REIT Guidelines. The Manager has a lower internal gearing threshold of 45% as a pre-emptive 
measure to provide a buffer as compared to the minimum regulatory requirement. 
Sunway  REIT  maintains  ample  debt  headroom  against  both  the  threshold  imposed  by  the  Listed  REIT  Guidelines  and  
the Manager’s internal threshold. As at 31 December 2025, Sunway REIT has a balance debt headroom of approximately 
RM1.1 billion to support growth initiatives. 
Sunway REIT drew down RM300 million in borrowings during the financial year to fund the acquisition of AEON Mall Seri 
Manjung  in  July  2025,  as  well  as  to  finance  progress  claims  for  the  refurbishment  of  the  old  wing  of  Sunway  Carnival   
Mall and the redevelopment of Sunway Pier.
 
During  the  year,  Sunway  REIT  also  repaid  RM600  million  of  borrowings  using  proceeds  from  the  disposal  of  Sunway  
university & college campus. Consequently, gearing improved, declining by 2.0% from 41.4% to 39.4% as at 31 December 
2025.
The  Manager  plans  to  optimise  the  gearing  in  the  short-term  to  support  opportunistic  yield-accretive  acquisitions  
and  AEIs.  Over  the  longer  horizon,  the  Manager  strives  to  maintain  the  gearing  level  at  below  45%  and  reviews  the  
opportunity  to  undertake  equity  financing,  when  there  are  potential  new  acquisitions  or  when  market  conditions  are  
conducive.
The  resilience  of  Sunway  REIT’s  capital  management  was  underpinned  by  a  diversified  financing  profile  comprising   
loans and debt securities, in both local and foreign currencies. This provides greater flexibility in funding structure over 
the short and medium-term.
Refinancing risk was moderated by Sunway REIT’s solid credit profile and robust balance sheet, coupled with the strong 
support from reputable financiers to Sunway Group. Sunway REIT recorded a strong interest service cover ratio of 4.0 
times for FY2025, well above the debt covenant level.
During the financial year, the corporate credit rating and program-level ratings have been re-affirmed by RAM Rating 
Services  Berhad.  The  strong  ratings  are  a  testament  to  Sunway  REIT’s  credit  fundamentals  and  favourable  market

position, with a prime and diversified asset and tenant mix, substantial financial flexibility and healthy debt coverage as 
factors lending strengths to the ratings. With the ratings, Sunway REIT will be looking to tap the debt capital markets in 
efforts to further optimise its capital structure and financing profile.
The  Manager  has  successfully  refinanced  borrowings  of  various  maturities  totalling  RM1.7  billion  during  the  financial  
year. As at 31 December 2025, the weighted average debt maturity of Sunway REIT stood at 1.6 years.
In reducing exposure to potential interest rate movement, Sunway 
REIT  continues  to  adhere  to  its  internal  policy  to  ensure  fixed  rate  
borrowings constitute at least 30%. The Manager has increased the 
fixed  rate  borrowings  of  Sunway  REIT  to  56%  as  at  31  December  
2025  to  capitalise  on  the  attractive  fixed  rate  borrowings  in  the  
first  half  of  2025  in  view  of  uncertainties  on  the  implementation  
of  tariff  by  the  United  States.  For  FY2025,  Sunway  REIT  continued  
the record as one of the lowest average cost of debt amongst the 
M-REITs at 3.79%.
In  the  near-term,  the  Manager  envisages  to  keep  a  balanced  
fixed  and  floating  rate  borrowings  and  continue  to  monitor  for  
opportunities  to  lock  in  favourable  fixed  rates  with  longer  tenures  
in view of the attractive Malaysian Government Securities (“MGS”)

ISSB STATEMENT
This   Statement   focuses   on   climate-   and   sustainability-related   
risks   and   opportunities,   specifically   Energy   Management   and   
Tenant  Satisfaction,  that  may  influence  the  Trust’s  value  creation,  
financial position, financial performance and cash flows. Disclosures 
on Business   Performance   risks   and   opportunities   are   provided   
separately in Sunway REIT Sustainability Report 2025.
BASIS OF PREPARATION
Compliance with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards
This  Statement  has  been  prepared  in  accordance  with  the  IFRS  
Sustainability Disclosure Standards - IFRS S1 and IFRS S2, as issued by 
ISSB and is aligned with Bursa Listing Requirements. 
Connectivity with Financial Statements
This  Statement  should  be  read  in  conjunction  with  Sunway  REIT’s  
audited   financial   statements   which   are   prepared   in   accordance   
with   the   Listed   REIT   Guidelines   in   Malaysia,   Malaysian   Financial   
Reporting   Standards   (“MFRS”),   IFRS   Accounting   Standards,   and   
Sunway   REIT   Sustainability   Report   2025.   The   sustainability-   and    
climate-related financial disclosures follow the same reporting entity 
and  organisational  boundary  as  the  audited  financial  statements,  
unless otherwise specified.
REPORTING BOUNDARY
The  reporting  boundary  covers  Sunway  REIT  and  its  subsidiaries  
(“Sunway  REIT”  or  “the  Trust”).  This  includes  all  28  assets  located  in  
Malaysia,  which  Sunway  REIT  holds  full  equity  interest,  consistent  
with  the  boundary  applied  in  the  audited  financial  statements.  The  
equity  share  approach  is  applied  consistently  for  greenhouse  gas  
(“GHG”) emissions and other climate-related metrics.
The    presentation    currency    of    the    sustainability-related    and     
climate-related   financial   disclosures   is   Ringgit   Malaysia   (“RM”),    
which  aligns  to  the  presentation  currency  used  in  the  consolidated  
financial  statements.  Unless  specified  otherwise,  all  amounts  are  
rounded to the nearest thousand. 
Changes During the Reporting Period 
There   was   one   acquisition   and   one   disposal   that   affected   the   
reporting boundary during the financial year: 
• Acquisition of AEON Mall Seri Manjung 
   The   sustainability-   and   climate-related   information   for   this    
asset is included from the acquisition date.
• Disposal of Sunway university & college campus 
 Disclosures  relating  to  this  asset  have  been  excluded  from  the  
reporting period following its disposal.
The  acquisition  of  SOVO  unit  at  Kiara  163  does  not  affect  the  
reporting   boundary   as   it   is   reported   under   an   existing   asset,   
Sunway 163 Mall. Aside from these changes, the reporting boundary  
remained unchanged throughout the reporting period.
First Time Adoption and Transition Reliefs
FY2025  is  the  first  annual  reporting  period  in  which  Sunway  REIT  
applies   IFRS   S1   together   with   continued   application   of   IFRS   S2.   
Sunway REIT has adopted both Standards in full and has not applied 
the  optional  climate  first  transition  relief  that  would  limit  IFRS  S1  
application to climate-related information.
FORWARD LOOKING
Preparation   of   sustainability-related   information   involves   the   use   
of    estimates,    forward-looking    assumptions    and    management    
judgement, particularly in assessing sustainability- and climate-related 
financial  effects,  transition  pathways  and  the  magnitude  and  timing  
of  risks  and  opportunities.  These  estimates  are  inherently  uncertain  
and  may  evolve  in  response  to  changing  economic,  regulatory  and  
environmental conditions. Further detail on specific assumptions and 
uncertainties is provided in later sections of this Statement.
ABOUT THIS STATEMENT
This  is  the  International  Sustainability  Standards  Board  (“ISSB”)  Statement  of  Sunway  REIT  for  
the  financial  year  from  1  January  2025  to  31  December  2025.  It  outlines  how  the  Trust  identifies,  
manages  and  reports  its  material  sustainability  and  climate-related  risks  and  opportunities  in  
accordance with IFRS S1 – General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability related Financial 
Information and IFRS S2 – Climate-related Disclosures. The information presented in this Statement 
is  intended  to  help  users  of  general  purpose  financial  reports  to  understand  how  these  matters  
may  reasonably  be  expected  to  affect  Sunway  REIT’s  cash  flows,  access  to  finance  and  cost  of  
capital over the short, medium and long-term.
For  more  information  on  the  boundary  of  GHG  Emissions,  please  
refer to pages 46 and 134 in SR 2025.
