ISSB Statement
The   Board   of   Directors   (“BOD”)   holds   overall   responsibility   for   
overseeing   sustainability-   and   climate-related   matters.   They   are   
supported  by  the  Sustainability  Committee  (“SC”),  which  provides  
strategic    direction,    reviews    sustainability    priorities    and    targets,    
and  monitors  progress  against  the  Trust’s  medium  and  long-term  
objectives,  including  its  Net  Zero  Carbon  Emissions  2050  roadmap.  
Sustainability   considerations   are   incorporated   into   Sunway   REIT’s   
broader governance arrangements and are applied with Bursa Listing 
Requirements and the Malaysian Code on Corporate Governance.
The  SC,  comprising  two  members  of  the  Board,  meets  biannually  to  
deliberate  on  sustainability  strategies,  review  material  sustainability  
issues  and  assess  the  adequacy  of  resources  allocated  to  address  
these   matters.   The   Committee   also   provides   oversight   on   the   
integration of sustainability considerations into business planning and 
operational processes. 
Prior    to    the    establishment    of    the    Sustainability    Department,    
sustainability  matters  were  overseen  by  a  dedicated  Sustainability  
Officer,   who   was   supported   by   the   Sponsor,   Sunway   Berhad,   
in    driving    foundational    sustainability    initiatives.    In    FY2023,    the    
Sustainability   Department   was   formally   established   to   take   over   
these  responsibilities.  The  department  now  leads  the  day-to-day  
coordination   of   sustainability   matters,   embedding   sustainability   
considerations  across  operations,  supporting  regulatory  compliance,

and facilitating communication between the Board, the Sustainability 
Committee, management, and business segments. 
Sunway   REIT   exercises   structured   and   robust   oversight   over   its   
sustainability-  and  climate-related  risks  and  opportunities  through  
both Board level and Committee level governance mechanisms. These 
governance  activities  reflect  Sunway  REIT’s  continued  emphasis  on  
integrating  sustainability  and  climate  considerations  into  strategic  
decision  making  and  ensuring  effective  management  oversight  of  
emerging risks and opportunities.
SUSTAINABILITY GOVERNANCE
Sunway REIT has established a sustainability governance framework that provides clear oversight, accountability and effective decision-making 
for  the  management  of  material  sustainability  and  climate  matters.  Governance  of  sustainability  is  anchored  at  Board  level  and  integrated  
across management and operational functions to ensure structured and consistent oversight of sustainability and climate-related issues.

Sunway  REIT  performed  a  double-materiality  assessment  in  FY2024  
covering  selected  economic,  environmental,  social  and  governance  
(“EESG”)   topics   to   evaluate   both   impact   materiality   and   financial   
materiality.  This  assessment  supports  the  Trust’s  decision  making  
processes   and   informs   the   identification   of   sustainability-   and    
climate-related   risks   and   opportunities   that   may   be   financially   
material  to  the  Trust’s  short,  medium  and  long-term  prospects.
Material  topics  that  may  affect  the  Trust’s  prospects  are  integrated  
into  the  Trust’s  risk  register  and  monitored  through  established  risk  
management  processes  aligned  with  the  Trust’s  short,  medium  and  
long-term   time   horizons   to   support   connected   information   and   
ongoing oversight.
RISK MANAGEMENT
Risk     management     plays     a     central     role     in     Sunway     REIT’s     
strategic   and   operational   resilience.   The   Trust   operates   within   
a    dynamic    environment    shared    by    evolving    climate    realities,    
regulatory    developments,    market    expectations    and    escalating     
sustainability-related  requirements.  Rising  electricity  costs,  potential  
carbon    pricing    mechanisms,    tightening    sustainability    disclosure    
standards  heighten  the  need  for  robust  governance  and  structured  
oversight of sustainability- and climate-related risks.
In        FY2025,        Sunway        REIT        identified        three        material         
sustainability-related     risks     –     Business     Performance,     Energy     
Management and  Tenant  Satisfaction  –  which  are  fully  integrated  
in  the  Trust’s  risk  management  framework.  These  risks  are  mapped   
to the Trust’s existing risk structure as follows:
Climate-related   risks   are   overseen   under   Climate   Change   Risk, 
ensuring alignment between climate specific insights and the Trust’s 
overarching risk governance processes.

systematic  process  for  identifying,  assessing,  prioritising,  managing  
and monitoring risks, which includes sustainability- and climate-related 
risk management.

ISSB Statement
Oversight is exercised by the Board, supported by RMC and SC, ensuring that sustainability- and climate-related risks are embedded into Sunway 
REIT’s broader governance and management processes.
To support consistent and comparable risk evaluation, Sunway REIT applies the risk parameters that assess financial and non-financial impacts, 
likelihood of occurrence and control effectiveness.
Risk 
Identification
Sustainability-  and  climate-related  risks  were  identified  using  input  from  double-materiality  assessment  conducted  in  
FY2024, external market and regulatory signals. These risks include both physical climate-related risks and transition risks 
associated with the shift to a lower-carbon economy.
Risk 
Assessment 
and 
Prioritisation
Each  risk  is  evaluated  based  on  its  likelihood  of  occurrence  and  potential  magnitude  of  impact,  using  Board-approved  
impact and likelihood risk parameters.
The identified sustainability- and climate-related risks are assessed together with financial and operational risks using the 
same set of risk parameters to support consistent prioritisation and oversight.
Sustainability-related  opportunities  are  also  incorporated  within  the  key  business  risks  section  and  evaluated  alongside  
other strategic opportunities to support value creation.
Risk 
Monitoring 
and Reporting 
Key sustainability- and climate-related risks are monitored through periodic updates via the risk registers and aggregation

CLIMATE-RELATED RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES
The  Jeffrey  Sachs  Center  on  Sustainable  Development  (“JSC”)  was  engaged  to  conduct  an  updated  climate  Value-at-Risk  (“VaR”)  assessment  
in  FY2024  covering  all  28  properties  within  Sunway  REIT’s  portfolio.  This  assessment  supported  the  identification  of  climate-related  risks  and  
opportunities by providing a comprehensive understanding of how climate change could affect the Trust’s portfolio and operations over short, 
medium and long-term horizons that align with strategic planning and risk oversight. The process considers both physical and transition risks and 
is aligned with the Trust’s risk management framework to ensure consistent evaluation and oversight.
Climate-Related Risks 
The VaR assessment evaluates:
• Physical risks, including acute events (such as extreme rainfall or flooding) and chronic changes (such as rising temperatures or long-term 
shifts in weather patterns) that may disrupt operations, damage assets, or increase operating and insurance costs.
 Given  Sunway  REIT’s  Malaysian  operating  context,  the  physical  climate  risk  assessment  prioritised  hazards  with  the  greatest  potential  
to  materially  affect  properties,  which  are  sea  level  rise  and  intensified  rainfall.  Sea  level  rise  elevates  coastal  flooding  risk,  while  
heavier  rainfall  increases  the  likelihood  of  flash  flooding  and  water  seepage.  Accordingly,  Direct  Rainfall  Damage  risk  and  Riverine  /   
Rainfall-Driven  Flooding  risk  were  selected  to  enable  clearer  estimation  of  potential  financial  effects  and  to  guide  risk  adaptation  and  
mitigation planning.
• Transition risks, including changes in policy, market expectations, technology pathways, and reputational factors that may influence energy 
costs, capital requirements, regulatory compliance and the competitiveness of Sunway REIT’s assets.
 The  primary  quantifiable  transition  risk  for  Sunway  REIT  relates  to  its  exposure  to  potential  changes  in  energy-related  policy  and  
associated electricity costs.
These climate-related risks are monitored through the Trust’s established risk management framework and mapped to existing risk categories for 
consistent monitoring, mitigation and escalation to relevant governance bodies.

These  opportunities  support  progress  against  the  climate-related  metrics  and  targets,  particularly  Scope  2  GHG  emission  intensity  and  Annual  
Renewable Energy Consumption, and contribute to long-term value creation.

Current Financial Effects
Energy management has a measurable effect on Sunway REIT’s operating cost structure, capital expenditure planning and financing profile. 
Electricity is one of the Trust’s largest operating expenses, accounting for approximately 19% of total operating expenses (RM45 million) in FY2025. 
These  costs  relate  solely  to  landlord  controlled  consumption  and  exclude  tenant  controlled  usage.  Given  their  scale  and  variability,  electricity  
expenses remain a material driver of operating expenditure and a central focus of ongoing efficiency and cost management initiatives.
Energy-related capital expenditure arises from planned retrofitting works and asset level upgrades forming part of the Trust’s long-term strategy  
to  improve  energy  performance.  In  addition,  Sunway  REIT’s  sustainability-linked  financing  arrangements,  which  incorporate  Building  Energy  
Intensity (“BEI”) performance metrics, create a direct linkage between energy performance outcomes and financing costs.
No material financial loss attributable to energy management was recorded during the reporting year, supported by stable electricity supply and 
ongoing operational optimisation efforts.

Significant Areas of Uncertainty
Future  financial  and  operational  outcomes  related  to  Sunway  REIT’s  
energy   management   activities   are   subject   to   several   areas   of   
uncertainty.  These  uncertainties  may  affect  the  timing,  magnitude  
and reliability of projected cost savings, capital expenditure plans and 
the achievement of energy-related targets.
Energy price volatility
Malaysia’s  energy  prices  are  influenced  by  fuel  costs,  prevailing  
market   conditions   and   tariff   structures.   Fluctuations   in   these   
inputs   may   lead   to   variability   in   operating   expenditure   and   
create  uncertainty  in  forecasting  savings  from  energy  efficiency   
initiatives.
Evolving regulatory requirements
Potential  amendments  to  the  EECA  and  other  related  regulation  
requirements   that   may   alter   compliance   thresholds,   reporting   
obligations     and     building     performance     requirements.     Such     
changes could affect the scope, timing and scale of future capital 
investment and may result in incremental operating or compliance 
costs.
Technological development and commercial availability
The  pace  of  technological  advancement  and  the  availability  of  
energy  efficient  systems  and  renewable  energy  solutions  may  
affect  the  performance,  cost  and  feasibility  of  planned  upgrades.  
Actual   outcomes   may   differ   from   projections   if   technologies   
evolve  more  slowly,  more  rapidly  or  at  different  cost  levels  than  
anticipated.
These  uncertainties  may  result  in  outcomes  that  differ  from  the  
Manager’s   current   expectations.   Estimates   will   continue   to   be   
reviewed   and   refined   as   regulatory   developments,   technological   
trends and market conditions evolve.
Capacity to Adjust or Adapt Strategy and Business Model
Sunway   REIT’s   energy   management   strategy   is   designed   with    
sufficient flexibility to adjust and respond to uncertainties associated 
with energy price changes, regulatory developments and technological 
changes.  The  Manager  maintains  several  adjustment  pathways  that  
allow  recalibration  of  operational  practices  and  capital  investment  
plans as external conditions evolve.
One  key  adjustment  pathway  is  the  potential  investment  in  BESS  to  
strengthen  operational  resilience.  BESS  is  a  large  scale  rechargeable  
battery system that stores electricity during periods of lower demand 
and   discharges   it   when   demand   or   tariff   prices   are   higher.   This    
supports load balancing, enhances backup capability and strengthens 
grid   stability,   enabling   the   Manager   to   optimise   its   operational   
response  to  changes  in  energy  prices,  regulatory  requirements  and  
emerging technologies.
Collectively,  these  adjustment  pathways  enhance  the  resilience  of  
Sunway  REIT’s  strategy  and  business  model  by  enabling  flexibility  in  
energy  procurement,  asset  level  system  upgrades  and  long-term  
capital  planning.  This  ensures  that  the  Trust  remains  well  positioned  
to   navigate   evolving   market   expectations,   regulatory   shifts   and   
technological    developments    while    safeguarding    financial    and    
operational stability.
Metrics and Targets
Sunway  REIT  uses  two  key  metrics  to  monitor  operational  efficiency  
and  to  assess  progress  against  its  energy  management  strategy:  
Building     Energy     Intensity     and     Green     Building     Certification     
Coverage  (%).  These  metrics  are  selected  for  their  relevance  to  the   
Trust’s energy consumption profile, operational control and exposure 
to energy-related risks.
Building Energy Intensity (“BEI”) 
BEI is the primary metric used to assess energy performance across the 
Retail, Office and Hotel portfolios. The target and baseline are sourced 
from  Malaysia  Green  Building  Index  (“GBI”)  and  benchmarked  against  
GBI Non-Residential Existing Building (“NREB”) Retail v1.1 rating tool. 
BEI is calculated as a segment-level average and applies only to assets 
where Sunway REIT has operational control over energy consumption. 
As such, the metric excludes: 
•                Sunway Pier, which is undergoing redevelopment; and
•    SunCity   Ipoh   Hypermarket   and   six   hypermarket   properties   
which  are  under  triple  net  lease  arrangements,  where  utilities  
consumption is tenant-controlled.
BEI  targets  have  not  been  established  for  the  Industrial  &  Others  
segment, as the Trust does not have operational control over energy 
consumption in these assets.
Further  details  on  BEI  performance  and  progress  against  targets,  
please  refer  to  Goal  1,  Transforming  Our  Portfolio  To  Low-Carbon  
Assets in SR 2025.
To  align  with  the  Intergovernmental  Panel  on  Climate  Change  
(“IPCC”) objective of a 45% reduction in carbon emission intensity 
by  2030  and  its  1.5°C  decarbonisation  trajectory,  Sunway  REIT  
has   established   intensity   based   BEI   reduction   target   of   4%    
year-on-year   from   2022   through   2030   for   its   Retail,   Office   
and  Hotel  segments.  The  target  forms  part  of  Sunway  REIT’s  
Sustainability Goals and Commitments since 2022 and supports 
the Trust’s longer-term transition towards net zero emissions.

SOCIAL-RELATED RISKS & OPPORTUNITIES
Sunway   REIT   operates   in   a   tenant-driven   property   market   where   occupancy   performance   and   income   stability   depend   on   sustained    
tenant  confidence  in  the  quality,  functionality  and  relevance  of  its  assets.  Across  the  Retail,  Office,  Hotel,  Industrial  &  Others  segments,  tenant  
perceptions  of  value  increasingly  extend  beyond  location  and  rental  rates  to  include  building  performance,  service  reliability,  safety  standards,  
digital readiness and environmental sustainability.
Recognising these evolving expectations, Sunway REIT views tenant satisfaction not merely as an operational output but as a core sustainability 
indicator  that  reflects  its  ability  to  manage  environmental,  social  and  governance  (“ESG”)  risks  and  opportunities.  Tenant  satisfaction  risk  is  
embedded  into  the  Trust’s  risk  management  framework  and  monitored  under  Tenant  Concentration  Risk  and  Tenant  Renewal  Risk,  enabling  
structured oversight of potential impacts on occupancy, rental income and long-term portfolio competitiveness.
Risks and Opportunities
The  assessment  of  tenant  satisfaction  risks  and  opportunities  highlights  factors  such  as  rising  operating  costs,  outdated  facilities,  inefficient  
building performance and reduced footfall, all of which may weaken Net Property Income (“NPI”) and asset valuations if left unaddressed. 
At  the  same  time,  consistently  high  tenant  satisfaction  presents  meaningful  opportunities  by  strengthening  portfolio  stability,  supporting   
resilient operating cash flows and enhancing Sunway REIT’s ability to deliver sustainable long-term returns to unitholders.
Sunway REIT is committed to obtain green building certifications for 100% of its portfolio by 2034. This metric covers existing properties and 
future acquisitions, with newly acquired properties are required to either be green-certified-ready or obtain certification within three years 
post-acquisition.
Progress  against  the  green  building  certification  target  is  tracked  annually.  The  steady  increase  in  certified  assets  reflects  ongoing   
certification  efforts  and  the  integration  of  green  building  standards  into  redevelopment  and  asset  enhancement  projects.  The  Manager  
expects the certification coverage to continue rising as more assets undergo certifications.
Target and Progress
The metric is calculated based on the percentage of green-certified GFA relative to the total portfolio GFA. The measurement approach and 
boundaries have remained consistent across reporting periods, with no restatements required. All properties within Sunway REIT’s portfolio 
are included in the calculation, except for assets that were disposed during the reporting year.

SR
In  practice,  decisions  relating  to  property  development  and  AEIs  require  a  careful  balance  between  capital  deployment,  operational  continuity  
and future income potential. Upgrading building systems and refurbishing operating assets can entail temporary revenue disruption (e.g. partial 
closures, tenant displacement or reduced footfall), significant upfront capex that may place short-term pressure on gearing, and execution risks 
(schedule delays and cost overruns). For new developments, the Manager also weighs uncertainty around the timing and level of future income 
streams, which are sensitive to market conditions and leasing performance.
The  same  strategic  lens  applies  to  adopting  green  building  standards.  Higher  upfront  capital  outlays  and  incremental  operating  expenditures  
(including recurring certification and recertification registration costs, consultant engagements and audits) are considered alongside the internal 
capability required to execute (e.g. dedicated sustainability personnel and enhanced data management systems).
Trade  off  evaluations  are  concluded  by  comparing  short-term  costs  and  risks  with  expected  long-term  outcomes,  including  lower  utility  
consumption,  improved  compliance  readiness,  enhanced  tenant  experience  and  stronger  positioning  with  sustainability  focused  investors  
and  financiers.  These  structured  assessments  drive  AEI  prioritisation  and  timing,  the  selection  of  performance  standards  in  project  scopes,  
the  sequencing  of  assets  with  the  most  material  efficiency  opportunities,  and  the  coordination  of  tenant  access  to  protect  critical  trading   
periods-ensuring sustainability related risks and opportunities are embedded in resource allocation and portfolio planning.
Impacts on Business Model, Value Chain and Financial Performance
Sunway REIT’s business model depends on the quality and competitiveness of its assets and on stable tenant relationships. Tenant satisfaction 
may  influence  leasing  outcomes,  operating  cost  profiles  and  capital  allocation.  As  a  result,  sustainability-related  actions  today  (e.g.  AEIs,  Green  
Building  Certifications,  etc.)  are  already  visible  in  cash  flows  and  investment  property  balances,  while  planned  redevelopments  and  efficiency

Financial Effects
Current Financial Effects 
Tenant  satisfaction  has  a  direct  influence  on  Sunway  REIT’s  revenue,  operating  cash  inflows  and  asset  value  preservation.  Rental  income  is  the  
sole source of revenue, totalling RM894 million for the financial year, with performance closely linked to occupancy levels, lease renewals and the 
quality of tenant relationships across the portfolio.
During  the  financial  year,  Sunway  REIT  did  not  experience  any  decline  in  revenue  attributable  to  tenant  satisfaction.  While  there  were  some   
tenant-related financial losses, these were not material to the Trust’s financial performance.
To  sustain  tenant  experience  and  asset  performance,  the  Trust  continued  to  invest  in  AEIs,  rectification  and  sustainability-related  upgrades.  
Collectively, stable rent collection, rental rebates and ongoing efficiency upgrades supported operating cash inflows, neutral-to-positive effects 
on the financial position. 
During  the  reporting  period,  no  impairment  indicators  were  identified,  supported  by  stable  tenant  metrics  and  the  results  of  regular  property  
revaluations.  Tenant  satisfaction  did  not  give  rise  to  material  balance-sheet  risk  but  it  continues  to  be  monitored  as  a  key  factor  in  preventing  
future asset value erosion.
Anticipated Financial Effects 
Looking  ahead,  tenant  satisfaction  is  expected  to  remain  a  key  driver  of  Sunway  REIT’s  revenue  stability,  cash  flows  and  long-term  asset  
competitiveness. 
In  the  short  (<2  years)  to  medium-term  (2-5  years),  higher  investing  cash  outflows  are  anticipated  as  the  Trust  progresses  with  planned  AEIs,  
deploy  efficiency  technologies  and  advances  initiatives  under  the  Green  Building  Roadmap.  These  investments  are  expected  to  be  funded  
primarily through borrowings and, where appropriate, operating funds. 
Rental rebates are expected to remain around 0.5% of total revenue over the short to long-term, subject to market conditions and the outcomes

of ongoing tenant engagement efforts. 
Over the medium (2-5 years) to long-term (>5 years), ongoing capital investments and service quality enhancements are anticipated to improve 
asset  efficiency,  moderate  operating  costs  and  strengthen  tenant  appeal,  thereby  supporting  occupancy  and  renewals,  stabilising  income  and  
contribute to long-term asset value preservation.

Capacity to Adjust or Adapt Strategy and Business Model
Sunway REIT demonstrates a strong capacity to adjust to uncertainties arising from tenant satisfaction by embedding resilience within its portfolio 
structure, operating model, financial management and governance processes. Tenant satisfaction is treated as a forward-looking sustainability 
factor that influences income stability, asset relevance and long-term value creation, rather than solely as an operational metric.

Financial Capacity & 
Risk Absorption
Sunway REIT’s diversified asset base reduces reliance on any single tenant group or sector. Integrated township assets 
generate natural footfall and demand, supporting tenant performance even during market fluctuations.
Structured  and  recurring  tenant  engagement  enable  early  identification  of  dissatisfaction  drivers,  such  as  operating  
costs, building performance and amenities. These insights allow timely operational responses, including targeted building 
upgrades, refinement of tenant mix, service-quality enhancements and cost efficiency initiatives. This feedback-driven 
approach reduces the risk of dissatisfaction escalating into vacancies, lower renewals or income disruption.
The Trust’s established track record of implementing AEIs and redevelopment provides flexibility to modernise facilities, 
improve  sustainability  performance  and  meet  evolving  tenant  expectations,  particularly  energy  efficiency,  building  
quality  and  green  building  certification.  This  reduces  exposure  to  long-term  obsolescence  risk  and  supports  the  
relevance and competitiveness of portfolio assets over time.
Tenant-related  sustainability  risks  are  reviewed  at  Senior  Management  and  Board  levels,  ensuring  they  inform  capital  
allocation  and  business  planning.  Trade-offs  between  short-term  financial  pressures  and  longer-term  asset  value  are  
explicitly evaluated, promoting disciplined resource allocation and consistent portfolio wide responses. 
Reflecting  the  nature  of  the  assets,  adaptability  is  considered  across  medium  and  long-term  horizons.  The  Trust  is  
positioned to respond to scenarios such as prolonged economic slowdowns, increased competition, shifts in occupier 
sustainability  expectations  and  external  disruptions  affecting  tenant  operations.  These  scenarios  inform  planning  
assumptions  and  investment  priorities,  strengthening  preparedness  for  changing  market  conditions  and  supporting  
the resilience of the business model.
Prudent capital management and adherence to regulatory gearing thresholds provides financial headroom to absorb 
temporary  income  pressures  when  tenant-related  risks  materialise.  This  allows  the  Trust  to  offer  short-term  rental  
support during pandemic and economic stress, continue essential capex and sustainability upgrades, and avoid reactive 
decisions such as forced disposals or deferred maintenance that could weaken future performance.

Metrics and Targets
Sunway  REIT  has  established  a  minimum  annual  Tenant  Satisfaction  
Score   target   of   80%,   effective   from   FY2025.   As   this   is   a   newly   
introduced  target,  no  revisions  or  restatements  required  during  the  
reporting period. The target applies on an annual basis, with no defined 
base year or interim milestones. It is informed by peer benchmarking 
across  the  Malaysian  REIT  industry.  The  definitions  and  calculation  
methods used to set and monitor this target are applied consistently 
across reporting periods to support comparability over time. 
Tenant Satisfaction Score
The  Tenant  Satisfaction  Score  is  a  quantitative  metric  derived  
from structured satisfaction surveys administered.
The metric is calculated as the proportion of “Satisfied” and “Very 
Satisfied”  responses  relative  to  the  total  number  of  responses  
received.  Responses  are  collected  using  a  defined  rating  scale  
(e.g. 1-5 or categorical responses ranging from “Very Dissatisfied” 
to    “Very    Satisfied”).    The    metric    is    assessed    against    the    
established 80% performance target and is subjected to limited 
external assurance covering the survey process controls and the 
calculation  of  the  metric.  The  assurance  scope  did  not  extend  
to   evaluating   individual   tenant   responses   or   the   underlying   
perceptions reported by respondents.

It serves as a leading indicator of relationship health with tenants 
and plays a role in assessing potential impacts on renewal rates, 
operational costs and overall portfolio performance.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE BOARD
The  Board  is  committed  to  fostering  an  effective  corporate  governance  culture  and  
ensuring that Sunway REIT’s strategic plan supports long-term value creation. 
The Board provides effective leadership and strategic direction to the Manager and Sunway 
REIT,  ensures  the  Management  performs  against  established  mission,  vision,  purpose   
and strategic goals.

The primary functions and roles of the Board include, but are not limited to: 
(i)   Integrating   considerations   of   sustainability   with   emphasis   on   the   aspects   of   
environment,   social   and   governance   (“ESG”)   and   ensuring   sustainable   business   
growth in order to create sustainable long-term value creation for the Company and 
Sunway REIT;
(ii)  Overseeing  and  evaluating  the  conduct  and  performance  of  Sunway  REIT  against  
budgets;
(iii)  Monitoring  progress  of  the  implementation  of  the  strategies,  budgets,  plans  and  
policies of the Company and Sunway REIT;
(iv)  Overseeing  the  conduct  of  Sunway  REIT’s  assets  to  evaluate  whether  they  are  
properly managed to achieve its targeted returns;
(v)   Identifying   principal   risks   of   the   Company   and   Sunway   REIT   and   ensuring   the   
implementation  of  appropriate  internal  control  systems  to  mitigate  and  manage  
these   risks.   The   Board   through   the   Risk   Management   Committee,   sets,   where   
appropriate,  objectives,  performance  targets  and  policies  to  manage  the  key  risks  
faced by the Company and Sunway REIT;
(vi)  Considering  and  approving  the  Management’s  recommendations  on  key  issues,  
including assets acquisitions and divestments, funding options, asset enhancement 
initiatives, property development activities and significant capital expenditures;
(vii)   Reviewing   the   adequacy   and   integrity   of   the   internal   control   systems   and   
management  information  systems  of  the  Company  and  Sunway  REIT,  including  
systems   for   compliance   with   applicable   laws,   regulations,   rules,   directives   and   
guidelines;
(viii) Ensuring that proper and effective control systems are in place for compliance with 
applicable laws and regulations. The Board also sets the disclosure and transparency 
standards  for  the  Company  and  Sunway  REIT  and  ensures  that  its  obligations  to  
unitholders of Sunway REIT are understood and met;
(ix) Overseeing the performance of CEO / Executive Director and Key Senior Management 
and  ensuring  an  effective  succession  plan  for  key  positions  within  the  Company,  
including  the  appointment,  training  and  development,  remuneration  and,  where  
appropriate, replacement of senior management;
(x) Approve and recommend income distribution amounts payable to the unitholders of 
Sunway REIT to the trustee of Sunway REIT (the “Trustee”); and
(xi)    Overseeing    the    development    and    implementation    of    the    investor    relations    
programme or unitholder communications policy for Sunway REIT; and
(xii)  Ensuring  that  the  sustainability  strategies,  priorities  and  targets  of  Sunway  REIT,  as  
well as its performance against these targets, are communicated to the unitholders 
and stakeholders of Sunway REIT.
In fulfilling its fiduciary duties, the Board is guided by its Board Charter. The Board Charter 
clearly defines the roles and responsibilities of the Board, the Board Chairman, definitions 
and scope of duties for independent and non-independent directors, separation of powers 
between the Chairman and the CEO as well as the mandated duties for Board Committees. 
SEPARATION OF POWERS
As  set  out  in  the  Board  Charter,  there  is  a  balance  of  power  and  authority  between  the  Chairman  and  the  CEO  with  a  clear  division  of  
responsibilities  between  the  running  of  the  Board  and  the  business  of  the  Company  and  Sunway  REIT  respectively.  The  roles  of  the   
Chairman and CEO of the Manager are held by two separate individuals. 
The  Chairman  of  the  Board,  Tan  Sri  Amirsham  Bin  A  Aziz,  provides  leadership  to  the  Board  and  ensures  its  effectiveness  in  all  aspects  
of  its  role.  He  leads  the  Board  in  setting  its  agenda  and  governance  priorities,  facilitates  constructive  engagement  between  the  Board  
and  Management  on  strategic,  operational,  financial  and  risk  matters,  and  ensures  that  Directors  are  furnished  with  timely  and  accurate  
information for sound decision-making. 
The CEO position is held by Mr. Derek Teh Wan Wei, who was appointed on 1 December 2025. As a non-Director CEO, he is responsible for 
the  day-to-day  management  and  strategic  execution  of  Sunway  REIT’s  operations.  He  provides  leadership  to  the  Management  team  in  
achieving strategic and operational goals, implements a robust risk management framework, and collaborates with the Board in formulating 
and executing strategies, policies, and decisions approved by the Board.
The distinct responsibilities of the Chairman and CEO are clearly outlined in the Board Charter of the Manager, which is publicly available on 
Sunway REIT’s website at www.sunwayreit.com.

REMUNERATION
The Board emphasises the importance of fair and competitive remuneration packages to attract, retain, and motivate Directors and key Senior 
Management of the Manager in driving Sunway REIT’s long-term growth objectives. The remuneration framework is designed to reflect each 
individual’s qualifications, experience, responsibilities, performance, and contributions to Sunway REIT’s long-term growth objectives.
The determination of remuneration for the Directors and key Senior Management is undertaken by the Manager, and not by Sunway REIT. 
The  annual  Directors’  fees  for  Non-Executive  Directors  are  subject  to  shareholders’  approval  at  the  Manager’s  AGM.  All  remuneration  
decisions are made in accordance with, and guided by, the Remuneration Policy.
The  remuneration  for  Non-Executive  Directors  is  determined  based  on  prevailing  market  trends,  time  commitment  and  additional  Board  
and  Committee  responsibilities  assumed  at  the  Board  and  Committee  levels.  The  remuneration  package  comprises  a  fixed  annual  fee,  
committee  fees  and  meeting  allowances.  Non-Executive  Directors  are  also  entitled  to  reimbursement  of  reasonable  travel  and  related  
expenses incurred in the discharge of their duties. 
In  line  with  the  NRC  TOR,  the  remuneration  of  Non-Executive  Directors  is  reviewed  at  least  once  every  three  years.  Following  the  last   
adjustment  in  2022,  a  comprehensive  review  was  undertaken  in  early  2026.  The  review  took  into  consideration  Sunway  REIT’s  significant  
growth   in   asset   size,   portfolio   diversification   and   increasing   transaction   complexity,   which   have   expanded   the   Board’s   oversight   
responsibilities across strategic, financial, investment and risk areas.
Directors  are  required  to  commit  greater  time  and  undertake  enhanced  responsibilities  at  both  Board  and  Committee  levels,  alongside

  In  carrying  out  its  mandate,  the  AC  assists  the  Board  in  reviewing,  evaluating  and  recommending  actions  on  matters  pertaining  to  
financial and accounting reporting, the adequacy and effectiveness of internal control systems, related party transactions and potential 
conflict-of-interest  situations.  Where  conflicts  arise  or  may  potentially  occur,  the  AC  assesses  the  circumstances  and  recommends  
appropriate mitigation or resolution measures to safeguard the best interests of Sunway REIT and its unitholders.
RISK MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE REPORT 
Operating in an increasingly dynamic and complex business environment, Sunway REIT recognises the importance of maintaining a robust 
system of internal controls supported by effective risk management practices. The Board remains firmly committed to overseeing these 
functions  by  establishing  a  clear  risk  appetite,  setting  the  tone  for  a  strong  risk-aware  culture,  and  ensuring  that  risk  considerations  are  
embedded in strategic and operational decision-making.
With the support of its Board Committees, the Board continuously reviews the adequacy and effectiveness of the processes in place for 
identifying, assessing, managing, and mitigating key risks. This includes regular monitoring of emerging risks, evaluation of control measures, 
and ensuring that appropriate mitigation strategies are implemented to safeguard the interests of unitholders and support the long-term 
sustainability of Sunway REIT.
RISK MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE (“RMC”)
The  RMC  assists  the  Board  in  overseeing  the  effectiveness  of  the  risk  management  framework,  including  the  policies  and  processes  
established  to  identify,  evaluate,  and  manage  key  risks  across  Sunway  REIT.  In  parallel,  the  AC  supports  the  Board  by  reviewing  and  
monitoring the adequacy and effectiveness of the internal control system, taking into account observations and recommendations from 
the independent external auditors.
The Board receives regular reports and updates from both Committees, ensuring that it remains well-informed of significant deliberations, 
key findings, and decisions arising from the delegated responsibilities under their respective purviews.
RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL CONTROL FRAMEWORK
The  governance  of  Sunway  REIT’s  risk  management  and  internal  controls  framework  rests  with  the  Board,  supported  by  the  RMC.  The  
Board  has  implemented  comprehensive  written  policies  and  procedures  governing  both  external  and  internal  audit  functions  to  ensure  
impartiality, independence, and effectiveness. These policies are subject to regular reviews to maintain their relevance and effectiveness. 
Annual  evaluations  of  internal  and  external  audit  partners  are  conducted  through  questionnaire-based  assessments  involving  the  Board  
and  Senior  Management  team  members.  The  Board  also  rigorously  reviews  financial  and  narrative  statements  in  accordance  with  best  
practices, drawing on the expertise of auditor for guidance. 
To  identify,  monitor,  and  manage  risk  effectively,  the  Board  has  established  a  structured  procedure.  It  conducts  periodic  reviews  of  the  
Manager’s risk management and internal control systems, assessing the effectiveness of material controls across financial, operational, and 
compliance areas. This includes the implementation and oversight of risk mitigation measures for material risks.
For specific risk information, please refer to the Statement of Risk Management and Internal Control (“SORMIC”) section of this report.
The Board holds ultimate responsibility for the governance of Sunway REIT’s risk management and internal control framework, with support 
from the RMC. To ensure the integrity and effectiveness of oversight mechanisms, the Board has established comprehensive written policies 
and procedures governing both internal and external audit functions. These policies are designed to uphold independence, objectivity, and 
operational  effectiveness,  and  are  reviewed  periodically  to  ensure  continued  relevance  in  line  with  evolving  regulatory  expectations  and  
best practices.
Annual assessments of the internal and external audit service providers are conducted through structured questionnaire-based evaluations 
completed by the Board and Senior Management. These assessments facilitate a holistic review of audit quality, performance, independence, 
and value creation.
In discharging its oversight responsibilities, the Board also undertakes rigorous reviews of financial and narrative statements. These reviews 
are conducted in accordance with applicable reporting requirements and leading governance practices, with the Board drawing upon the 
professional insights of the auditors to support sound and transparent disclosures.
To ensure the effective identification, monitoring, and management of risks, the Board has established a structured and systematic approach 
to  overseeing  Sunway  REIT’s  risk  management  and  internal  control  systems.  The  Board  conducts  periodic  reviews  of  the  Manager’s  risk  
management  framework  and  internal  control  processes,  assessing  the  adequacy  and  effectiveness  of  material  controls  across  financial,  
operational,  and  compliance  areas.  This  includes  ongoing  oversight  of  the  implementation  of  risk  mitigation  measures  to  ensure  that  
material risks are appropriately managed in line with the Board-approved risk appetite.

3. PERFORMANCE OF THE AC
 In line with good governance practices, the Board engages an independent professional consultant to undertaken a board effectiveness 
evaluation (“BEE”) once every 3 years, or as otherwise deemed necessary. As the recent independent BEE was conducted in 2024, the 
BEE for 2025 was undertaken internally and facilitated by the Company Secretarial team. 
 The assessment covered key areas of the AC’s responsibilities, with the results summarised below:
i. Composition and Governance
 The AC was acknowledged for its clear communication of expectations and its ability to obtain timely and adequate information to 
support effective oversight. AC members were recognised for possessing an appropriate mix of skills, qualifications, and financial 
literacy,  enabling  the  AC  to  discharge  its  duties  competently.  The  Chairman  demonstrated  strong  leadership,  commitment,  and  
deep  understanding  of  AC’s  mandate  and  members  expressed  confidence  in  addressing  complex  and  sensitive  matters  during  
deliberations.
ii. Information Flow and Meeting Effectiveness
  The  AC  ensured  efficient  meeting  processes,  with  agendas  and  papers  circulated  sufficiently  ahead  of  meetings  to  facilitate  
informed  discussion.  Meetings  were  conducted  in  a  structured  manner,  providing  adequate  time  for  deliberation  on  critical  and  
emerging issues. The Chairman fostered open discussion, encouraging input from members, Management, and both external and 
internal  auditors.  Recommendations  were  promptly  escalated  to  the  Board,  while  special  sessions  with  senior  management  were  
convened whenever necessary to provide deeper insights into business risks.
iii. Oversight of Financial Reporting and Audit Functions
 The AC demonstrated strong oversight of the financial reporting process and audit functions. AC members constructively engaged 
with Management and the auditors to ensure the integrity, accuracy and completeness of financial disclosures. Recommendations 
arising from the AC’s review were promptly elevated to the Board, and the Committee maintained a balanced and objective approach 
in addressing audit matters and significant judgements.
iv. Risk Oversight, Governance and Internal Controls
  The  AC  proactively  reviewed  key  business,  financial  and  reporting  risks,  provided  oversight  on  related  party  transactions  and  
conflict-of-interest disclosures. The whistleblowing mechanism was periodically reviewed and assessed to be effective. The AC also 
engaged with other Board Committees on intersecting areas of responsibility and reviewed tax governance to mitigate financial and 
reputational risks, demonstrating a sound governance framework and commitment to ethical oversight.
v. Overall Effectiveness and Reporting Line
  The  AC  maintained  transparent  and  constructive  communication  with  the  Board,  effectively  escalating  unresolved  or  significant  
issues  and  ensuring  balanced  deliberations.  The  AC’s  findings  and  recommendations  facilitated  timely  and  informed  Board   
decision-making.
  The  annual  self  and  peer  evaluation  of  the  AC  confirmed  that  members  collectively  and  individually  fulfilled  their  responsibilities  
effectively.  AC  members  were  recognised  for  their  integrity,  active  participation,  and  problem-solving  capabilities,  constructive  input  
as well as their ability to manage differing views constructively. The AC demonstrated strong financial literacy, deep understanding of 
statutory reporting requirements, and sound knowledge of both financial and non-financial risks affecting Sunway REIT. AC members 
were consistently rated “Excellent” in their ability to evaluate information critically. 
 In conclusion, the AC was assessed to be effective in discharging its duties and responsibilities. The evaluation reaffirmed the AC’s strong 
leadership,  rigorous  oversight,  and  commitment  to  continuous  improvement  in  governance,  risk  management  and  internal  control  
practices.  The  AC  continues  to  uphold  high  standards  of  professionalism,  competence,  and  integrity,  contributing  meaningfully  to   
the overall governance structure of Sunway REIT.

5. SUMMARY OF ACTIVITIES
 The AC carried out the following activities during FY2025:
A. Financial Reporting
(a) Quarterly Financial Results
 At the AC meetings held on 3 February 2025, 13 May 2025, 11 August 2025 and 10 November 2025, the AC reviewed and discussed 
the  quarterly  management  accounts  and  financial  results  with  Management.  The  AC  ensured  that  all  relevant  regulatory  and  
accounting disclosures requirements, as well as applicable financial reporting standards were fully complied with. 
 During each meeting, the CFO presented the quarterly financial reports and confirmed that:
i.  The  accounting  policies  and  methods  of  computation  adopted  were  consistent  with  those  used  in  the  previous  audited  
financial statements;
ii. There were no significant or unusual matters other than those disclosed in the unaudited financial results;
iii. Sunway REIT continued to operate as a going concern; and
iv. All relevant accounting standards, regulatory requirements and legal obligations had been duly complied with in preparing the 
quarterly financial statements.
  The  AC  scrutinised  the  quarterly  financial  results  to  ensure  the  appropriateness  of  the  accounting  treatments  applied  and  the  
accuracy  of  the  reported  figures.  The  CFO  highlighted  all  material  transactions,  key  accounting  adjustments  and  provisions  
recognised during the period. 
 Following its review, the AC was satisfied that the quarterly unaudited financial results had been prepared in accordance with:
i. The applicable financial reporting standards;
ii. The Bursa Listing Requirements;
iii. The Listed REIT Guidelines; and
iv. The provisions of the Deed dated 20 May 2010, the Supplemental Deed dated 10 June 2010, the Amended and Restated Deed 
dated  18  September  2019  and  Second  Amended  and  Restated  Deed  dated  7  April  2025  (“Deed”)  entered  into  between  the  
Manager and RHB Trustees Berhad (“Trustee”).
 The AC concluded that the quarterly results presented a true and fair view of Sunway REIT’s financial position, financial performance 
and  cash  flows  for  each  respective  quarter.  The  AC  subsequently  recommended  the  quarterly  results  to  the  Board  for  approval  
prior to release to Bursa Malaysia.
(b) Accounting standards and other relevant regulatory requirements
  During  the  financial  year,  the  AC  was  briefed  on  the  amendments  to  legislation,  accounting  standards  and  other  regulatory  
requirements that may have a financial or compliance impact on Sunway REIT.
 At the meeting on 3 February 2025, the AC was updated on the following changes to the Bursa Listing Requirements:
i. New Issue of Securities:
• Enhanced transparency requirements for fund-raising activities and the Employee Share Scheme framework.
• Strengthened  disclosure  obligations  relating  to  the  remuneration  of  chief  executive,  aimed  at  codifying  current  market  
practices.
ii. Sustainability Reporting Requirements
• Alignment of sustainability reporting obligations with the National Sustainability Reporting Framework (NSRF) to promote 
consistency and comparability.
• Mandatory  conduct  of  physical  or  hybrid  general  meetings  to  enhance  shareholder  engagement  and  facilitate  broader  
participation.
• Strengthened  accountability  measures  for  Recognised  Principal  Advisers,  including  enhanced  disclosure  requirements  in  
public documents.
 At the meeting held on 10 November 2025, the AC was updated on the following key regulatory developments:
i. Revised Fee Structure for REIT Managers by Securities Commission Malaysia
• The  Securities  Commission  Malaysia  announced  a  revision  to  the  annual  fee  structure  for  REIT  Managers,  effective   
1 January 2026, with a 3-year transitional concession period from 2026 to 2028 to facilitate industry adjustment.
ii. Amendments to the Bursa Listing Requirements in relation to Continuing Disclosures and Islamic Capital Market
• Enhanced transparency requirements relating to corporate rescue mechanisms under the Companies Act 2016. 
• Introduction  of  exemptions  for  certain  related  party  transactions  involving  joint  venture  partners,  subject  to  specified  
conditions. 
• Improvements to the efficiency, consistency and transparency of Shariah screening review processes.
  In  addition,  the  External  Auditors  presented  their  annual  Transparency  Report,  prepared  in  accordance  with  the  requirements  of  
the Audit Oversight Board and the International Standard on Quality Management, which provided insights into their quality control 
processes, governance structure and audit methodology.

 On 20 March 2025, the AC met with the External Auditors and Management to deliberate on the audited financial statements for 
the  financial  year  ended  31  December  2024  (“AFS2024”).  During  the  meeting,  the  AC  was  briefed  on  the  audit  status,  significant  
audit findings, key audit matters, the review of internal controls and the External Auditors’ proposed audit opinion. 
  Based  on  the  significant  audit  findings,  the  AC  approved  the  inclusion  of  the  following  key  audit  matter  in  the  External  Auditors’

B. External and Internal Audit Reports
(a) External Auditors
 The AC held discussions with the External Auditors, Messrs BDO PLT (“BDO”), on several occasions during the year:
i. Key Regulatory Developments
 On 20 March 2025, the AC, together with Management, reviewed and deliberated on the Audit Report relating to the audit of 
the financial statements for FY2024. The External Auditors confirmed their professional independence in respect to the audit 
engagement. 
  During  the  meeting,  the  External  Auditors  presented  the  audit  status,  significant  audit  findings,  key  audit  matters,  financial  
reporting developments and the proposed audit opinion. They reported that no non-compliance with laws and regulations or 
fraud-related matters had come to their attention in the course of their audit. BDO also confirmed that they had reviewed the 
internal audit reports and performed the necessary procedures in accordance with ISA610: Using the Work of Internal Auditors. 
   Both   the   AC   and   Management   confirmed   to   the   External   Auditors   that   they   were   not   aware   of   any   instances   of    
non-compliance with laws and regulations, nor any significant fraud-related matters during the financial year.
ii. Audit Planning Memorandum and Transparency Report
  On  11  August  2025,  the  External  Auditors  briefed  the  AC  on  the  Audit  Planning  Memorandum  (“APM”)  for  FY2025.  The  APM  
outlined the External Auditors’ engagement scope and reporting responsibilities, audit approach, materiality and performance 
materiality  threshold,  areas  requiring  significant  auditor  attention,  engagement  team  composition,  reporting  timelines,  key  
deliverables and independence consideration, including audit and non-audit fees.
 The AC was also briefed on the establishment of system of quality management in compliance with International Standard on 
Quality Management 1 (“ISQM 1”), which governs audit quality, risk assessment and ongoing monitoring of audit engagements.
  In  addition,  the  External  Auditors  presented  their  Transparency  Report  2024,  which  highlighted  BDO’s  commitment  to  audit  
quality,  strong  governance  structure,  ethical  independence,  and  adherence  to  ISQM  1  and  ISQM  2.  The  report  detailed  how  
BDO’s  system  of  quality  management  (“SOQM”)  is  designed,  implemented  and  monitored  to  support  high-quality  audit  and  
assurance engagements. It also provided key indicators relating to audit practice capacity, independence safeguards, personnel 
competency,  training  investments  and  results  of  internal  and  external  quality  reviews,  demonstrating  continuous  efforts  to  
enhance audit quality and transparency for stakeholders.
  After  reviewing  the  nature,  scope  and  quantum  of  non-audit  services  rendered,  the  AC  was  satisfied  that  such  services  did  
not  give  rise  to  any  conflict  of  interest  and  that  the  External  Auditors’  independence  remained  intact.  The  AC  subsequently  
approved the proposed audit and non-audit fees.

  The  AC  held  two  private  sessions  with  the  External  Auditors  on  20  March  2025  and  11  August  2025,  without  the  presence  of

  The  AC  conducted  its  annual  assessment  of  the  performance  and  effectiveness  of  the  External  Auditors,  BDO.  The  AC

• Effective  engagement  and  communication,  supported  by  timely  meetings  and  candid  discussions  on  governance,  fraud  
controls and financial reporting matters.
• Strong  audit  quality  and  independence,  demonstrated  through  objective  assessment  of  accounting  standards,  rigorous

• Comprehensive understanding of Sunway REIT’s operations, which enhanced the relevance and quality of audit insights.

(b) Internal Audit
i. Internal Audit Plan
  On  3  February  2025,  the  AC  reviewed  and  approved  the  Internal  Audit  Department  (“IAD”)’s  internal  audit  plan  for  FY2025   
(“IA Plan FY2025”). The IA Plan FY2025 sets out the internal audit strategies, priorities and planned engagements for the year, 
and continues to adopt a risk-based audit approach. The audit planning process incorporated a review of the audit universe, 
input from Management and an assessment of key risks and exposures relevant to Sunway REIT’s operations. 
  The  IA  Plan  FY2025  was  developed  in  accordance  with  the  leading  practices  under  the  International  Professional  Practices  
Framework (“IPPF”) issued by the Institute of Internal Auditors (“IIA”), which includes the Global Internal Audit Standards and the 
IIA Code of Ethics.
 The AC reviewed and approved the internal audit areas for FY2025, which encompassed:
• Assurance:  Review  of  key  operational  processes  across  major  properties,  newly  acquired  properties  and  major  asset  
enhancement initiatives and property developments.
• IT  &  Cybersecurity:  Review  the  readiness  of  compliance  with  Guidelines  on  Technology  Risk  Management  issued  by  
Securities Commissions Malaysia, evaluate adherence to Hotels’ information technology (“IT”) general controls and review 
compliance with ISO27001 Information Security Management System standards.

6. INTERNAL AUDIT FUNCTION
  The  internal  audit  function  is  performed  in-house  and  undertaken  by  the  Manager’s  IAD.  The  main  role  of  the  internal  audit  function  is  
to  provide  the  AC  with  independent  and  objective  evaluation  of  the  adequacy  and  effectiveness  of  the  system  of  internal  controls,  risk  
management and governance framework of Sunway REIT. The IAD has undertaken regular and systematic reviews of the risk management 
and  internal  controls  system  so  as  to  provide  reasonable  assurance  that  risk  management  and  internal  control  systems  continues  to  
operate adequately and effectively at Sunway REIT.
 To uphold the independence and objectivity of the internal audit function, the IAD reports functionally to the AC and administratively to the 
CEO. The AC has explicit authority to communicate directly with the IAD and vice versa. The IAD also has direct, unrestricted access to the 
AC to highlight any issues of concern at any time. In addition, the IAD has unfettered access to the Manager and Sunway REIT’s documents, 
records, properties and personnel.
 The IAD is a member of the Malaysian Chapter of the IIA and adopts the International Standards for the Professional Practices of Internal 
Auditing (“IIA Standards”) laid down in the International Professional Practices Framework issued by the IIA. The IAD successfully completed 
its External Quality Assessment Review (“EQAR”) by KPMG in 2022 and it was concluded that the IAD continues to meet or exceed the IIA 
Standards in all key aspects. The next EQAR was planned to be carried out in year 2027.
 In order to ensure that the responsibilities of the IAD and the internal audit function were fully discharged, the AC had reviewed the Audit 
Plan FY2025, the adequacy of the scope and resources of the internal audit function as well as the performance of the IAD in undertaking 
its internal audit function during the financial year under review.
Details of the continuing education programmes attended by the Directors for FY2025 are available under the Board of Directors section of the 
Manager on Sunway REIT’s website at https://www.sunwayreit.com.
 Internal audit reports encompassing the audit findings together with the recommendations were presented to the AC on a quarterly basis. 
The  IAD  and  Management  were  responsible  for  ensuring  the  corrective  action  plans  had  been  carried  out  effectively  within  the  agreed  
timeframe and regular follow-up audits had been performed to ensure management actions had been effectively implemented.
  The  IAD  is  headed  by  Ms.  Khong  Shiyi  who  has  more  than  18  years  of  internal  audit  experience  and  reports  directly  to  the  AC  to  ensure  
impartiality and independence. She is a Certified Internal Auditor (“CIA”) by Institute of Internal Auditors. She holds a Bachelor of Commerce 
Degree majoring in Accounting from University of Melbourne and is a member of the CPA Australia and Chartered Accountant registered 
with the Malaysian Institute of Accountants (“MIA”).
 The IAD comprises 4 internal auditors, all of them have relevant tertiary and / or professional qualifications. The IAD provides independent 
and  objective  assessment  on  the  adequacy  and  effectiveness  of  the  internal  controls,  risk  management  and  governance  framework  of

BOARD RESPONSIBILITY 
The  Board  of  the  Manager  acknowledges  its  overall  responsibility  for  maintaining  an  effective  system  of  risk  management  and  internal  
control  that  supports  the  achievement  of  Sunway  REIT’s  strategic  objectives  while  safeguarding  unitholders’  interests  and  assets.  This  
responsibility encompasses reviewing the adequacy and effectiveness of the framework governing financial, operational, compliance and 
sustainability risks, including climate-related and technology-driven exposures.
The Board sets the risk appetite, approves risk policies, and ensures that appropriate governance structures and assurance mechanisms are 
in place. Oversight is exercised through the Risk Management Committee (“RMC”) and Audit Committee (“AC”), which report to the Board on 
a periodic basis. 
MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITY 
Management is accountable for implementing the risk management framework, policies and procedures approved by the Board. It identifies, 
evaluates, mitigates and monitors material risks across business and operational levels and reports significant matters to the RMC.
The  Management  promotes  a  culture  of  integrity  and  ethical  conduct  through  the  Code  of  Conduct,  clear  delegation  of  authority,  policy  
manuals,  and  continuous  communication.  It  ensures  that  employees  are  equipped  with  the  necessary  competencies  and  that  control  
responsibilities are clearly defined and embedded in day-to-day decision-making.
RISK MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORK 
Sunway  REIT’s  risk  management  framework  is  benchmarked  against  ISO  31000:2018  Risk  Management  Guidelines  and  incorporates  
principles  from  the  COSO  Enterprise  Risk  Management  framework.  The  framework  establishes  a  systematic  and  structured  process  for  
identifying, assessing and responding to risks at both fund and operational levels.
• Integrate risk management into strategic planning and performance management;
• Define clear governance roles under the three lines of defence model; and
• Strengthen accountability and promote proactive risk ownership.

INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEM
Sunway REIT’s internal control system is designed to provide reasonable, not absolute, assurance against material misstatement, financial loss or 
fraud. The system comprises policies, processes and behaviours that support achievement of strategic, operational and compliance objectives.
Key elements include:
• Clear strategic plans and budgets approved by the Board and reviewed regularly;
• Policies and procedures manuals covering key operations and regulatory compliance;
• Whistleblowing mechanism and independent reporting channels;
• Internal audit reviews based on a risk-based annual audit plan approved by the AC;
• Compliance review and updates by a dedicated compliance officer.
COMPLIANCE OFFICER
The  Manager  has  a  designated  Compliance  Officer  to  ensure  compliance  with  the  Deed  and  all  applicable  guidelines  issued  by  Securities  
Commission Malaysia and securities laws relating to Sunway REIT. The Compliance Officer monitors compliance based on the framework within

the  policy  manual  and  compliance  guidelines,  procedures,  guidance  and  assessment  questionnaires  that  are  in  place  for  compliance  with  the  
Deed, Listed REIT Guidelines, Securities Commission Licensing Handbook, Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 and Bursa Listing Requirements. 
AUDIT COMMITTEE AND INTERNAL AUDIT DEPARTMENT 
The AC, with the support of the internal audit department, is tasked by the Board with the duty of reviewing and monitoring the adequacy and 
effectiveness of the system of internal controls, risk management, and governance processes.
In  discharging  its  duties,  the  AC  relies  significantly  on  the  support  of  the  internal  audit  function,  which  carries  out  internal  audits  based  on  a  
risk-based  audit  plan  approved  annually  by  the  AC.  Based  on  these  audits,  the  AC  is  provided  with  periodic  reports  highlighting  observations,  
recommendations and management action plans in order to assist AC in the effective discharge of their roles and responsibilities. In addition, the 
AC reviews and deliberates on any matters relating to internal controls highlighted by the external auditors in the course of their statutory audit 
of the financial statements.

Metroplex Holdings Sdn. Bhd. (“Metroplex”) v RHB Trustees Berhad (as trustees for Sunway REIT) and Sunway REIT Management 
Sdn. Bhd. (collectively, the “Defendants”)
Metroplex  is  claiming  for  various  chattels  and  movable  items  which  were  allegedly  acquired  and  owned  by  Metroplex  but  not  
removed by Metroplex when the Defendants took possession of the hotel at Sunway Putra on 27 September 2011.
Since then, this case has proceeded through the High Court (which allowed Metroplex’s claim on liability), the Court of Appeal 
(which allowed the Defendants’ appeal and set aside the High Court’s decision), and then the Federal Court, which on 31 March 
2021 overturned the Court of Appeal’s Decision and reinstated the High Court’s Decision in favour of Metroplex. 
On  12  November  2024,  the  High  Court  delivered  its  judgment  on  the  assessment  of  damages  for  conversion  payable  by  the  
Defendants, on behalf of Sunway REIT, to Metroplex. However, on 9 December 2024, Metroplex appealed to the Court of Appeal 
against  part  of  the  High  Court’s  Judgment  on  Assessment,  which  assessed  the  damages  to  be  paid  by  the  Defendants  to  
Metroplex for the conversion of Metroplex’s operational chattels. On 10 December 2024, the Defendants appealed to the Court 
of Appeal against part of the High Court’s Judgment on Assessment, which assessed the damages to be paid by the Defendants 
to  Metroplex  for  the  tort  of  conversion  of  antiques  and  artworks.  On  13  December  2024,  the  Defendants  remitted  the  sum  
of RM8,087,684.45, which represented the amount payable under the High Court’s Judgment on Assessment on 12 November 
2024, to Metroplex. This sum included interest payable on the judgment amount calculated up to 13 December 2024 along with 
costs and allocatur fee.

1. FUND INFORMATION
  Sunway  Real  Estate  Investment  Trust  (“Sunway  REIT”  or  the  “Fund”)  is  a  Malaysia-domiciled  real  estate  investment  
trust  constituted  pursuant  to  a  deed  dated  20  May  2010,  a  supplemental  deed  dated  10  June  2010,  an  amended  and   
restated  deed  dated  18  September  2018  and  a  second  amended  and  restated  deed  dated  7  April  2025  (collectively   
referred  to  as  the  “Deed”)  between  Sunway  REIT  Management  Sdn.  Bhd.  (the  “Manager”)  and  RHB  Trustees  Berhad   
(the “Trustee”). The Fund was listed on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia Securities Berhad on 8 July 2010. 
  The  registered  office  of  the  Manager  is  located  at  Level  16,  Menara  Sunway,  Jalan  Lagoon  Timur,  Bandar  Sunway,  47500  
Subang Jaya, Selangor Darul Ehsan.
 The principal place of business is located at Level 15, Menara Sunway, Jalan Lagoon Timur, Bandar Sunway, 47500 Subang 
Jaya, Selangor Darul Ehsan. 
  Sunway  REIT  is  an  income  and  growth  fund  with  the  key  investment  objective  to  provide  unitholders  with  exposure  to  a  
diverse portfolio of authorised investments (pursuant to provisions of the Deed) that will provide stable cash distributions 
with  the  potential  for  sustainable  growth  in  net  asset  value  (“NAV”)  per  unit.  The  principal  investment  policy  of  Sunway   
REIT is to invest in retail, hospitality, office and other real estate assets, subject to the Securities Commission’s Guidelines 
on  Listed  Real  Estate  Investment  Trusts  (“Listed  REIT  Guidelines”).  The  principal  activities  of  the  subsidiaries  are  set  out

(b) Financial risk management objectives and policies

The  Manager  proactively  reviews  the  capital  management  of  the  Group  and  of  the  Fund  to  ensure  that  adequate  
financial resources are available for the working capital requirements, growing the Group’s and the Fund’s businesses 
and for income distributions whilst managing its interest rate risks (both fair value and cash flow), liquidity risk, foreign 
currency risk and credit risk. The Manager reviews and agrees policies for managing each of these risks and they are 
summarised below.
 Interest rate risk
 Interest rate risk is the risk that the fair value or future cash flows of the Group’s and the Fund’s financial instruments 
will fluctuate because of changes in market interest rates. The Group’s and the Fund’s interest rate risk arises primarily 
from  borrowings  at  floating  rates.  All  of  the  Group’s  and  the  Fund’s  borrowings  at  floating  rates  are  contractually   
re-priced monthly and quarterly. 
 The Manager manages the Group’s and the Fund’s interest rate exposure by monitoring a mix of fixed and floating 
rate borrowings. At the end of the reporting period, the Group’s and the Fund’s cross currency swap contracts are not 
affected  by  any  interest  rate  benchmarks  reforms.  Approximately  56%  (2024:  45%)  of  the  Group’s  and  62%  (2024:  
17%) of the Fund’s borrowings are at fixed rates of interest.
  The  interest  rate  profile  and  sensitivity  analysis  of  interest  rate  risk  have  been  disclosed  in  Notes  19  and  24  to  the  
financial statements.
Foreign currency risk
  Foreign  currency  risk  is  the  risk  that  the  fair  value  or  future  cash  flows  of  a  financial  instrument  would  fluctuate  
because of changes in foreign exchange rate.
  The  Group  and  the  Fund  are  not  significantly  exposed  to  foreign  currency  risk  as  all  of  the  Group’s  and  of  the  Fund’s  
transactions,  assets  and  liabilities  are  denominated  in  Ringgit  Malaysia  (“RM”)  except  for  the  Revolving  Loans  which  are  
denominated in United States Dollar (“Revolving Loans - USD”) as disclosed in Note 24(c) to the financial statements.
 The Revolving Loans - USD are hedged with cross currency swap contract. As such, fluctuation in USD is not expected 
to have any material effects to the financial performance and position of the Group and of the Fund.
5. CAPITAL AND FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT (CONT’D.)
(b) Financial risk management objectives and policies (cont’d.) 
Liquidity risk
  The  Manager  manages  the  Group’s  and  the  Fund’s  debt  maturity  profile,  operating  cash  flows  and  the  availability  
of  funding  so  as  to  ensure  that  refinancing,  repayment  and  funding  needs  are  met.  As  part  of  its  overall  liquidity  
management,  the  Group  and  the  Fund  maintain  sufficient  levels  of  cash  or  cash  convertible  investments  to  meet  
their working capital requirements. In addition, the Manager strives to ensure that the Group and the Fund maintain 
available banking facilities at a reasonable level to its overall debt position. As far as possible, the Group and the Fund 
raise committed funding from both capital markets and financial institutions and balances their portfolio with some 
short term funding so as to achieve overall cost effectiveness.
  At  the  end  of  the  reporting  period,  RM2,598,118,000  (2024:  RM1,736,966,000)  of  the  Group’s  and  RM878,118,000  
(2024:  RM506,966,000)  of  the  Fund’s  gross  borrowings  will  be  maturing  in  the  next  twelve  months  based  on  the  
carrying amount reflected in the financial statements. There will be no repayment risk for the maturing borrowings 
as the borrowings could be refinanced with the existing facilities backed by commitments from financial institutions.
 The analysis of financial instruments by remaining contractual maturities has been disclosed in Notes 24, 25, 26, 28 
and 29 to the financial statements.
Credit risk
  Credit  risk  is  the  risk  of  loss  that  may  arise  on  outstanding  financial  instruments  should  a  counterparty  default  on  
its obligations. The Group’s and the Fund’s exposure to credit risk arises primarily from trade receivables. For other 
financial assets (including cash and bank balances and derivatives), the Group and the Fund minimise credit risk by 
dealing exclusively with high credit rating counterparties.
  The  Group’s  and  the  Fund’s  objective  is  to  seek  continual  revenue  growth  while  minimising  losses  incurred  due  to  
increased  credit  risk  exposure.  The  Group  and  the  Fund  trade  only  with  recognised  and  creditworthy  third  parties.  
It  is  the  Group’s  and  the  Fund’s  policy  that  all  customers  who  wish  to  trade  on  credit  terms  are  subject  to  credit  
verification procedures. In addition, receivable balances are monitored on an ongoing basis with the result that the 
Group’s and the Fund’s exposure to bad debts is not significant. 
 The credit risk concentration profiles have been disclosed in Notes 17 and 18 to the financial statements.

6. REVENUE (CONT’D.)
(a) Rental income
 Rental income is derived from renting of retail and office properties to tenants and includes base rent, turnover rent 
and  service  and  promotion  charges  from  tenants.  Base  rent  and  service  and  promotion  charges  are  recognised  in  
profit or loss on a straight-line basis over the term of lease. Contingent rent such as turnover rent is recognised as 
income  in  the  profit  or  loss  on  an  accrual  basis  unless  recoverability  is  in  doubt,  in  which  case,  it  is  recognised  on  
receipt basis.
(b) Hotel master lease income
 Hotel master lease income is derived from leasing of hotel properties to hotel operators for a 10-year lease term and 
is recognised on accrual basis unless recoverability is in doubt, in which case, it is recognised on receipt basis.
 The hotel master lease income for Sunway Lagoon Hotel is derived based on the following rent formula:
 Total rent = The higher of variable rent or guaranteed rent 
 Variable rent = Base rent plus 70% of (hotel’s gross operating profit less master lease expenses)
 (i)  Base rent: 20% of the hotel’s gross operating revenue.
 (ii)  Gross operating profit: Hotel’s gross operating revenue less operating expenses. 
 (iii)  Master lease expenses: Base rent, reserve for furniture, fittings and equipment and hotel management fees.
  The  hotel  master  lease  agreement  for  Sunway  Resort  Hotel,  Sunway  Pyramid  Hotel  and  Sunway  Hotel  Seberang  
Jaya  has  been  renewed  on  7  July  2020  for  another  term  of  10  years,  commencing  from  8  July  2020,  with  the  rent  
formula of 90% of hotel’s gross operating profit (after accounting for reserve for furniture, fittings and equipment).  
Similarly,  Sunway  Putra  Hotel  and  Sunway  Hotel  Georgetown  has  renewed  its  hotel  master  lease  agreement  on   
30 August 2021 and 18 December 2024 respectively for another term of 10 years, commencing from 28 September 
2021 and 1 January 2025 respectively, with the rent formula of 90% of hotel’s gross operating profit (after accounting 
for reserve for furniture, fittings and equipment).
(c) Industrial rental income
 Industrial rental income comprises master lease income and rental income.
 The industrial master lease income is derived from leasing of an industrial premises to a lessee based on a triple net 
basis whereby all the property operating expenses, quit rent, assessment and insurance will be borne by the lessee, 
with  initial  term  of  approximately  17  years  expiring  on  31  December  2034  and  is  recognised  on  a  straight-line  basis  
over the term of lease unless recoverability is in doubt, in which case, it is recognised on receipt basis.
 The industrial rental income is derived from renting of industrial premises to tenants and are recognised in profit or 
loss on a straight-line basis over the term of lease. 
(d)  Education master lease income
  Education  master  lease  income  is  derived  from  leasing  of  an  education  premises  to  lessees  with  initial  term  of   
30  years  expiring  on  30  November  2048  at  a  predetermined  annual  rental  with  a  2.3%  annual  rental  increase  and  
is  recognised  on  a  straight-line  basis  over  the  term  of  lease  unless  recoverability  is  in  doubt,  in  which  case,  it  is  
recognised on receipt basis. The disposal of education premises was completed on 30 September 2025.
6. REVENUE (CONT’D.)
(e)  Car park rental income
 Car park rental income is derived from renting of the investment properties’ car park space to car park operators and 
is recognised on accrual basis unless recoverability is in doubt, in which case, it is recognised on receipt basis. The car 
park rental income is derived based on the following variable rent formula:

Variable rent = Base rent plus 95% of car park’s gross operating profit 
 (i)  Base rent: 20% of the car park’s gross operating revenue.
 (ii)  Gross operating profit: Car park’s gross operating revenue less base rent and operating expenses.
(f) Other operating income
 Other operating income mainly comprises rental from common area of the retail properties for promotional events 
and  is  recognised  on  the  accrual  basis  unless  recoverability  is  in  doubt,  in  which  case,  it  is  recognised  on  receipt  
basis. 
(g) Unbilled lease income receivable 
  Unbilled  lease  income  receivable  is  recognised  on  a  straight-line  basis  over  the  lease  term  pursuant  to  the  
requirements of MFRS 16 Leases.

(e) Methods of valuation
  The  Income  Approach  by  Investment  Method  involved  capitalisation  of  the  net  annual  income  stream  that  is   
expected  to  be  received  from  the  property  after  deducting  the  annual  outgoings  and  other  operating  expenses  
incidental to the property with allowance for void by using an appropriate market derived capitalisation rate.
  The  Income  Approach  by  Discounted  Cash  Flow  (DCF)  Method  incorporates  the  estimation  of  future  annual  cash  
flows over an investment horizon (5 years) from the valuation date by referencing to expected revenue growth rates, 
operating expenses and terminal value. The present value of future cash flow is then determined by the application 
of an appropriate discount rate to derive a net present value of the property as at the valuation date. It is assumed 
that the property is sold at the commencement of the terminal year of the cash flow at the expected rate of return 
of similar asset class.
 In undertaking the analysis, the valuer has used a wide range of assumptions for the property including the growth 
of hotel’s average room rates and other potential revenues during the holding year, projected occupancy, expense 
ratios / expected property expenses and other related expenses.
  As  the  investment  properties  are  commercial  and  income  generating  properties,  the  valuers  have  adopted  the  
market value as derived from the Income Approach as a more appropriate method supported by the market value as 
derived from the Comparison Approach.
